rationale.B: Model size does not give access to history the subagent never received.
rationale.C: Sandbox settings are inherited; history is not, by design.
rationale.D: They do not share history; there is no such toggle described.

stem: A developer wrote a 'format-tests' skill that is useful in every repository they work in, while a 'release-notes' skill only makes sense for one product repository shared by the team. Where should each skill live?

options.A: Both in the global skills folder on the developer's machine
options.B: format-tests in AGENTS.md, and release-notes as a hook in hooks.json
options.C: format-tests global; release-notes in the repository's .agents/skills/
options.D: Both in the product repository, so everyone gets both skills automatically

rationale.A: Teammates would not get release-notes with the repository.
rationale.B: Neither is a skill mechanism; rules and hooks serve different purposes.
rationale.C: Global skills in the CLI's home skills directory are shared across workspaces; workspace skills in .agents/skills/ travel with the repository.
rationale.D: Other repositories would not get format-tests.

stem: A team published a workspace skill for creating database migrations, but the agent rarely uses it when asked to 'add a column to the orders table'. The skill's body is excellent. What is the most likely issue?

options.A: The skill is too short; skills are chosen by the length of their instructions
options.B: The front-matter description does not say when to use the skill, so it is not selected
options.C: The skill must be converted into a subagent before the agent can call it
options.D: Skills only run when referenced in AGENTS.md by their exact file path

rationale.A: Selection is driven by the description, not body length.
rationale.B: Skills are declared with name and description front matter; the description is what lets the agent match a task to the skill.
rationale.C: Skills are used directly; conversion is unnecessary.
rationale.D: Skills are discovered from their directories, not only through rules.

stem: A multinational engineering organisation has dozens of reusable agent skills with approved instructions, scripts and documentation. Many teams need to discover and reuse them, and the platform team must control which version agents load by default and roll back quickly if a release misbehaves. What should they use?

options.A: Skill Registry: immutable skill revisions plus a default revision pointer
options.B: A shared Cloud Storage bucket of skill folders with object versioning enabled
options.C: Agent Designer templates that embed each skill's instructions
options.D: A Git repository per team, with each team copying skills they like into their own repo

rationale.A: Skill Registry stores skills with immutable revisions and a default revision pointer that can be changed to deploy or roll back a version.
rationale.B: Storage versioning is not discovery, and agents have no notion of a default revision.
rationale.C: Low-code agent templates are not a skill distribution mechanism for coding agents.
rationale.D: Creates the independent copies the platform team wants to avoid.

stem: Uploading a skill package to Skill Registry fails. The package is a 14 MB zip containing SKILL.md, helper scripts and a bundled 12 MB dataset used only by one script. What should you do?

options.A: Split the skill into two skills of 7 MB each that reference one another
options.B: Upload the package as a new revision, since revisions have higher size limits
options.C: Rename SKILL.md to README.md, because only README files are exempt from size limits
options.D: Keep the dataset outside the package and fetch it at run time, keeping the zip under 10 MB

rationale.A: Artificially splits one capability and complicates versioning.
rationale.B: Revisions are snapshots of the same package format and limits.
rationale.C: SKILL.md is required and there is no README exemption.
rationale.D: Skill Registry limits the zip file to 10 MB; large data should be referenced rather than bundled.

stem: A developer wants Claude Code and the Antigravity CLI on their machine to know how to scaffold, evaluate and deploy ADK agents on Google Cloud the recommended way, without writing those instructions themselves. What should they run?

options.A: agents-cli create, which adds deployment skills to the coding agents on the machine
options.B: agents-cli setup, which installs the Agents CLI skills into detected coding agents
options.C: agents-cli publish gemini-enterprise, which exposes the skills in the Gemini Enterprise UI
options.D: agents-cli playground, which teaches the coding agents by demonstrating each command

rationale.A: create scaffolds a new agent project from a template; it does not install skills.
rationale.B: agents-cli setup installs agents-cli and its skills into detected coding agents globally or per workspace.
rationale.C: publish registers a deployed agent with Gemini Enterprise.
rationale.D: playground starts a local agent playground for testing an agent.

stem: A team lets its coding agent drive Agents CLI while developing, but release engineers want the production deployment in the pipeline to run the same commands deterministically, with no model deciding what to do. How does Agents CLI support this?

options.A: Human mode: the same agents-cli commands run directly in scripts or a terminal
options.B: Recording the agent's session once and replaying the transcript in CI
options.C: A separate deployment-only CLI, because Agents CLI requires a coding agent to run
options.D: Agent mode with temperature zero, so the coding agent makes the same choices each time

rationale.A: Agents CLI supports agent mode (coding assistants run the commands using skills) and human mode (deterministic control running commands in terminals or scripts).
rationale.B: Replaying a transcript is not a supported, deterministic deployment mechanism.
rationale.C: The same CLI runs without a coding agent in human mode.
rationale.D: Still model-driven; the requirement is no model in the loop.

stem: A nightly release pipeline runs the Agents CLI deployment command on a build agent with no terminal attached. The job hangs for its full 60-minute timeout waiting for a confirmation prompt nobody can answer, and the deployment never happens. What should be added to the command?

options.A: The -i / --interactive flag, so the prompt is printed to the job log
options.B: The --no-wait flag, which answers confirmation prompts automatically
options.C: A preceding agents-cli login -i step inside the pipeline
options.D: The -y / --auto-approve flag, which skips prompts and uses defaults

rationale.A: Interactive mode enables prompts, which is the cause of the hang.
rationale.B: --no-wait returns without waiting for deployment completion; it does not approve prompts.
rationale.C: login requires interactive mode and does not remove deploy prompts.
rationale.D: Non-interactive mode (-y, --auto-approve, --yes) skips prompts and is suitable for CI/CD automation.

stem: An existing ADK agent built by hand has good logic but no deployment configuration, no CI/CD and no RAG setup. The team wants to add these using the standard templates without rewriting the agent code. Which command fits?

options.A: agents-cli scaffold upgrade, which installs the missing deployment files
options.B: agents-cli infra single-project, which generates CI/CD and RAG code
options.C: agents-cli scaffold enhance, which adds deployment, CI/CD or RAG scaffolding to a project
options.D: agents-cli create, which regenerates the project from a template over the existing code

rationale.A: upgrade moves a scaffolded project to a newer CLI version via three-way merge.
rationale.B: It provisions optional single-project infrastructure and IAM, not RAG scaffolding.
rationale.C: scaffold enhance enhances an existing project with deployment, CI/CD or RAG scaffolding without modifying agent logic.
rationale.D: create starts a new project; it would not preserve the hand-built structure.

stem: A team scaffolded its agent with an older Agents CLI version and has since customised several generated files. A new CLI version brings improved deployment templates. They want the improvements without losing their edits. What should they run?

options.A: agents-cli create into a new folder, then copy the customised files back by hand
options.B: agents-cli scaffold upgrade, which merges template changes with a three-way merge
options.C: agents-cli scaffold enhance, which overwrites generated files with the latest version
options.D: agents-cli update, which reinstalls skills and regenerates project templates

rationale.A: Manual and error-prone; upgrade exists for this.
rationale.B: scaffold upgrade updates projects to newer CLI versions using a three-way merge to preserve customisations.
rationale.C: enhance adds new scaffolding; it is not the version-upgrade path.
rationale.D: update force-reinstalls skills in coding agents; it does not merge project templates.

stem: A team wants every pull request that changes agent prompts to show whether evaluation results got better or worse than on main. Which Agents CLI commands support this?

options.A: agents-cli eval run on both versions, then eval compare on the two result files
options.B: agents-cli eval optimize on the pull request to replace the prompts automatically
options.C: agents-cli lint --fix on the prompt files to detect regressions
options.D: agents-cli run with a single prompt on each branch, compared by a reviewer

rationale.A: eval run chains generation and grading; eval compare compares two evaluation result JSON files.
rationale.B: optimize is experimental prompt optimisation, not a regression comparison.
rationale.C: Linting checks code quality, not agent behaviour.
rationale.D: One prompt is not an evaluation set, and manual comparison is not a gate.

stem: An agent's instructions have been hand-tuned for weeks and evaluation scores have plateaued. The team has a solid evaluation set and wants to try automated, metric-driven improvement of the prompts. Which Agents CLI capability is designed for this?

options.A: agents-cli eval analyze, which rewrites prompts for each failure cluster it finds
options.B: agents-cli eval dataset synthesize, which generates better prompts from traces
options.C: agents-cli scaffold enhance, which adds a prompt-tuning module to the project
options.D: agents-cli eval optimize, which iterates on prompts using the GEPA framework

rationale.A: analyze clusters failures to explain them; it does not rewrite prompts.
rationale.B: synthesize creates evaluation traces through user simulation, not improved prompts.
rationale.C: enhance adds deployment, CI/CD or RAG scaffolding.
rationale.D: eval optimize (experimental) optimises agent prompts using the GEPA framework for iterative improvement.

stem: A new agent project needs separate staging and production environments with Terraform-managed infrastructure and a pipeline in GitHub Actions or Cloud Build. The team wants the standard setup generated for them. What should they run?

options.A: agents-cli deploy --list
options.B: agents-cli publish gemini-enterprise
options.C: agents-cli infra setup-cicd
options.D: agents-cli infra single-project

rationale.A: Lists deployments; it does not create pipelines or environments.
rationale.B: Registers a deployed agent with Gemini Enterprise.
rationale.C: infra setup-cicd sets up CI/CD pipelines and Terraform infrastructure for staging and production using GitHub Actions or Cloud Build.
rationale.D: Provisions single-project infrastructure, not a staging and production pipeline.

stem: An ADK agent is deployed to Agent Runtime and passes evaluation. Business users should now be able to find and use it inside Gemini Enterprise. Which Agents CLI step completes this?

options.A: agents-cli run --url, which lists the agent in the Gemini Enterprise gallery
options.B: agents-cli deploy --target gemini-enterprise, which redeploys it there
options.C: agents-cli setup --workspace, which shares the agent with the workspace
options.D: agents-cli publish gemini-enterprise, which registers the deployed agent

rationale.A: run sends a single prompt to a local or deployed agent.
rationale.B: Deployment targets are Agent Runtime, Cloud Run or GKE; Gemini Enterprise is reached by publishing.
rationale.C: setup installs skills into coding agents.
rationale.D: publish gemini-enterprise registers a deployed agent with Gemini Enterprise, supporting A2A or ADK agent types.

stem: A newly installed Antigravity CLI plugin from another team introduces a hook that slows every edit. A developer wants to turn it off for a day while the owners investigate, without losing its configuration. What should they run?

options.A: agy plugin disable <name>, then agy plugin enable <name> once it is fixed
options.B: Delete hooks.json from the plugin folder by hand
options.C: /hooks to remove the hook from the running session
options.D: agy plugin uninstall <name>, then reinstall it once it is fixed

rationale.A: Plugins can be toggled with disable and enable without deletion.
rationale.B: Edits a managed package in place and may break its next update.
rationale.C: /hooks inspects active hooks; the durable toggle is disabling the plugin.
rationale.D: Uninstall removes it completely, losing local configuration.

stem: A 'release-notes' subagent should be able to run `git log` but nothing else in the terminal, while the parent agent keeps its broader command permissions. Which subagent configuration addresses this?

options.A: Rely on inheritance: subagents always get stricter command permissions than parents
options.B: Set commandExecutionPolicy in the subagent's front matter to allow only git log
options.C: Put 'only run git log' in the subagent's description field
options.D: Disable the terminal sandbox for the subagent so policies apply correctly

rationale.A: Subagents inherit the parent's allowed command prefixes; tightening needs explicit configuration.
rationale.B: Subagent front matter supports tools, model and commandExecutionPolicy to shape what the subagent may execute.
rationale.C: The description is for selection and documentation, not enforcement.
rationale.D: Removing the sandbox reduces isolation and does not restrict commands.

stem: A support agent's failures only appear several turns into a conversation, but the team's evaluation set contains single-turn prompts. They lack recorded multi-turn conversations. Which Agents CLI capability helps build a multi-turn evaluation set?

options.A: agents-cli eval grade, which extends single-turn cases into conversations
options.B: agents-cli eval metric list, which adds multi-turn cases for each metric
options.C: agents-cli eval dataset synthesize, which simulates users to generate multi-turn traces
options.D: agents-cli playground, which saves sessions as evaluation sets automatically

rationale.A: grade scores traces against metrics; it does not generate them.
rationale.B: It lists available metrics; it does not create cases.
rationale.C: eval dataset synthesize (experimental) synthesises evaluation traces via model-based user simulation for multi-turn conversations.
rationale.D: The playground is interactive testing; it does not synthesise datasets.

stem: Developers in one repository use different coding agents (Antigravity, Claude Code and others). The team wants one source of project conventions that each agent reads, rather than maintaining divergent rules files. What is the most practical approach?

options.A: Standardise on a single coding agent and forbid the others
options.B: Encode conventions as hooks so every agent must follow them
options.C: Keep conventions in AGENTS.md and reference it from agent-specific files
options.D: Maintain separate full rules files per agent and sync them by hand each sprint

rationale.A: Organisationally costly and unnecessary for sharing conventions.
rationale.B: Hooks intercept actions; they cannot express coding conventions.
rationale.C: A shared AGENTS.md read as rules keeps one source of truth; agent-specific files can reference it.
rationale.D: Divergence is exactly the problem to avoid.

stem: A platform team registered 300 skills in Skill Registry. Agents in production should pick relevant skills based on the user's request rather than loading all 300 into context, and teams should be able to create and search skills through an agent. What provides this?

options.A: Intent-based discovery from Skill Registry, plus the built-in gcp-skill-registry skill
options.B: Agent Gateway semantic governance, which injects matching skills into prompts
options.C: A nightly job that copies the ten most-used skills into each agent image
options.D: Loading all 300 SKILL.md files into the system prompt at session start

rationale.A: Skill Registry lets agents dynamically discover and load relevant skills by intent, and ships a managed gcp-skill-registry skill to create, search and manage skills.
rationale.B: Semantic governance evaluates tool calls against policy; it does not distribute skills.
rationale.C: Static, stale, and ignores the user's intent.
rationale.D: Wastes context and cost; the registry exists to avoid this.

stem: Developers want to trigger a workspace skill named 'format-tests' explicitly instead of relying on the agent to pick it. What does the Antigravity CLI provide?

options.A: An MCP tool generated from the skill that developers call through /mcp
options.B: Workspace skills are converted into slash commands, so /format-tests runs it
options.C: A hook named format-tests that developers trigger with a keyboard shortcut
options.D: A subagent spawned from the skill with ctrl+k

rationale.A: /mcp manages MCP servers; skills are not converted into MCP tools.
rationale.B: Workspace skills in .agents/skills/ auto-convert to slash commands such as /format-tests.
rationale.C: Hooks are event interceptors, not user-invoked commands.
rationale.D: ctrl+k approves pending subagent actions; it does not run skills.

stem: A defence contractor is building an agent that summarises classified-adjacent engineering reports. Policy requires that prompts and outputs never leave the company's Google Cloud project and VPC, and the security team must control the serving environment. Quality needs are moderate. Which model strategy fits?

options.A: Call a proprietary model through its serverless model-as-a-service endpoint, relying on standard terms
options.B: Run inference on developer laptops with a quantised model and sync results to the project
options.C: Fine-tune the largest available proprietary model so it no longer needs external calls
options.D: Self-deploy an open model from Model Garden into the project, served inside the VPC

rationale.A: Serverless MaaS does not give the team control of the serving environment the policy requires.
rationale.B: Moves sensitive data onto endpoints outside the controlled environment.
rationale.C: Tuning does not move serving into the project, and the largest model is not needed for moderate quality.
rationale.D: Self-deployed Model Garden models run in your project and VPC network with full control of the serving environment, unlike serverless model-as-a-service offerings.

stem: A marketplace's multi-agent system receives 40 million messages a day. Every message first passes a router that picks one of six specialist agents; the planner agent that follows needs strong reasoning. Latency and cost are dominated by the router today. What model design is best?

options.A: A rules-only router with no model and no planner, because models are too slow at this volume
options.B: A small, fast model for the router and a larger LLM only for the planner
options.C: A small model for the planner and the large LLM for the router, since routing is the entry point
options.D: The most capable LLM for both router and planner, so routing mistakes never happen

rationale.A: Drops the reasoning capability the planner provides.
rationale.B: Matching model size to task keeps the high-volume classification step cheap and fast while keeping reasoning quality where it matters.
rationale.C: Inverts the needs: planning requires reasoning, routing does not.
rationale.D: Pays top-tier cost and latency on 40 million simple classifications.

stem: A healthcare analytics company already runs a large GKE platform with GPU node pools and a mature SRE team. It wants to serve a Gemma model for an internal agent at steady, high throughput, reuse its existing cluster tooling, and tune the serving stack itself. Which option fits?

options.A: Run the model inside the agent's Cloud Run container on CPU only to avoid GPUs
options.B: Use a serverless model-as-a-service endpoint so the SRE team no longer operates the model
options.C: Deploy the model to Agent Runtime as an agent so it scales with the agent
options.D: Serve Gemma on GKE with vLLM on GPU node pools

rationale.A: CPU-only inference for steady high throughput is slow and costly.
rationale.B: Removes the control the team explicitly wants to keep and reuse.
rationale.C: Agent Runtime hosts agents, not a tunable model-serving stack.
rationale.D: Google documents serving Gemma on GKE with vLLM on supported GPUs, which fits a team that wants to reuse and tune its own cluster.

stem: A startup must choose a model for a legal-drafting agent. It expects to fine-tune on its own corpus, wants the option to move serving between clouds later, and has an ML team comfortable operating models. Top-tier reasoning is less important than control. Which consideration most favours an open-weights model?

options.A: Weights can be tuned, inspected and served anywhere, avoiding lock-in to one provider's API
options.B: Open-weights models never incur infrastructure costs because the weights are free
options.C: Open models always outperform proprietary models on legal reasoning benchmarks
options.D: Proprietary models cannot be used for drafting documents under any licence

rationale.A: Open weights give control over tuning, portability and serving, which are the startup's stated priorities.
rationale.B: Serving open models costs compute; the weights being free is not the same as free inference.
rationale.C: Not true in general, and reasoning quality was not the priority.
rationale.D: Incorrect; the decision is about control and portability, not a blanket prohibition.

stem: A small product team wants to prototype an agent this week using a partner model available in Model Garden. They have no one to manage GPUs or endpoints and traffic will be unpredictable. Which deployment style is appropriate?

options.A: A GKE cluster with vLLM, autoscaled on request queue depth
options.B: A self-deployed endpoint on dedicated GPUs, sized for peak traffic from day one
options.C: The serverless model-as-a-service offering, which needs no manual deployment
options.D: A Compute Engine VM with the model weights downloaded manually

rationale.A: Operationally heavy for a team with no one to run it.
rationale.B: Requires endpoint management and pays for idle GPUs during a prototype.
rationale.C: MaaS offerings are serverless and don't require manual deployment, unlike self-deployed models.
rationale.D: Manual serving is the most operational effort of all options.

stem: An architect must evaluate Google, partner and open models side by side before selecting one for a new agent, and wants a single place in Google Cloud to discover and try them. Where should they start?

options.A: Agent Registry, which lists every model available to agents in the organisation
options.B: Skill Registry, whose skills each wrap one foundation model for comparison
options.C: Model Garden, the catalogue of foundation models from Google, partners and open source
options.D: Agent Garden, the managed endpoint that serves every model on demand

rationale.A: Agent Registry catalogs agents, tools, skills and MCP servers, not foundation models.
rationale.B: Skill Registry stores agent skills, not models.
rationale.C: Model Garden is described as a library of 200+ foundation models from Google, partners and open source for discovery and experimentation.
rationale.D: Agent Garden provides samples; it is not a model catalogue or serving endpoint.

stem: A travel agent assistant uses one large model for everything. Profiling shows 70% of calls are short extraction tasks (dates, cities, passenger counts) and 30% are itinerary planning. Leadership wants a 50% cost cut without hurting planning quality. What should you propose? (Choose two.)

options.A: Keep the large model for planning and measure planning quality before and after
options.B: Cache every planning response by destination for 30 days
options.C: Switch everything to the smallest model and add 'think carefully' to the planning prompt
options.D: Double the context window so extraction and planning can share one call
options.E: Route extraction calls to a smaller, cheaper model validated on an extraction eval set

rationale.A: Protects the quality-sensitive path and proves it did not regress.
rationale.B: Itineraries depend on dates and preferences; long-lived caching returns wrong plans.
rationale.C: Prompting does not recover reasoning capacity lost by the model swap.
rationale.D: Larger contexts raise cost and do not address the model mismatch.
rationale.E: Moves the high-volume simple work to a model sized for it, verified by evaluation.

stem: A developer is building an ADK agent and wants to chat with it, inspect each event, tool call and state change, and run evaluation cases locally before anything is deployed or billed for hosting. What should they use?

options.A: adk deploy cloud_run --with_ui, then test in the deployed UI
options.B: The Agent Designer preview pane in Gemini Enterprise
options.C: adk deploy agent_engine, then use the Agent Runtime console
options.D: adk web, which starts the local development UI on localhost

rationale.A: Deploys and bills hosting before local iteration is done.
rationale.B: Agent Designer builds no-code agents, not local ADK code.
rationale.C: Also a deployment; the requirement is local testing first.
rationale.D: adk web runs the local dev UI (port 8000) with event inspection and an Eval tab; nothing is deployed.

stem: An ADK agent frequently receives identical product questions. The team wants to return a cached answer without calling the LLM when an exact match exists, and otherwise proceed normally. Where should this logic go, and how does it short-circuit?

options.A: A before_model_callback that returns an LlmResponse on a cache hit, skipping the model call
options.B: A before_tool_callback that returns the cached answer as the tool result
options.C: An after_model_callback that returns the cached answer instead of the model's response
options.D: An after_agent_callback that deletes the model's answer when a cached one exists

rationale.A: Returning an LlmResponse from before_model bypasses the actual LLM call; returning None proceeds normally.
rationale.B: Tool callbacks wrap tool execution, not the model call.
rationale.C: By then the LLM call has already happened and been paid for.
rationale.D: Runs after the agent finishes; the model call already occurred.

stem: An ADK agent has a `transfer_funds` tool. The business rule is that transfers above 10,000 must never execute from this agent, whatever the model decides. The team wants the check in code and a clear result returned to the model. What is the best implementation?

options.A: An after_tool_callback that reverses the transfer when the amount was above the limit
options.B: A before_tool_callback that returns an error dict for large transfers, skipping execution
options.C: An instruction in the agent prompt stating that transfers above 10,000 are forbidden
options.D: A before_model_callback that removes the word 'transfer' from user messages

rationale.A: The transfer has already executed; compensating afterwards is not prevention.
rationale.B: Returning a dict from before_tool skips the tool and uses the returned value as the result, enforcing the rule deterministically.
rationale.C: Prompt rules can be ignored or bypassed; the requirement is enforcement in code.
rationale.D: Crude input filtering that breaks legitimate requests and misses rephrasings.

stem: A company has 30 ADK agents. Security wants the same PII-redaction and prompt-logging policy applied to all of them, maintained in one place, rather than copying callbacks into every agent definition. What does the ADK documentation recommend?

options.A: A LoopAgent that wraps each agent and retries until no PII appears
options.B: An ADK Plugin that implements the policy once and is registered for all agents
options.C: A before_model_callback copied into each of the 30 agent definitions
options.D: A shared system instruction that asks every agent to redact PII

rationale.A: Workflow agents orchestrate sub-agents; they are not a policy mechanism.
rationale.B: The docs recommend Plugins over individual callbacks for security guardrails and policies because they are more modular and flexible.
rationale.C: Works, but duplicates the policy the team wants to maintain centrally.
rationale.D: Instructions are not deterministic redaction.

stem: A shopping assistant built with ADK must remember a user's preferred currency across all of that user's future sessions, keep a feature flag shared by all users of the app, and hold a scratch value only for the current invocation. Which state keys fit?

options.A: app:currency, user:feature_flag and scratch
options.B: temp:currency, feature_flag and app:scratch
options.C: user:currency, app:feature_flag and temp:scratch
options.D: currency, app:feature_flag and user:scratch

rationale.A: Swaps user and app scopes, leaking one user's currency to everyone.
rationale.B: temp: is discarded after the invocation, so the currency is forgotten.
rationale.C: user: is shared across a user's sessions, app: across all users and sessions, and temp: is discarded after the invocation.
rationale.D: An unprefixed key is session-scoped, and user: persists the scratch value indefinitely.

stem: A developer loads a session with the session service, sets `session.state['cart_total'] = 42` in application code outside any tool or callback, and later finds the value missing after a restart with the Agent Platform session service. Why, and what is correct?

options.A: Direct mutation bypasses event history; write through context.state or a state_delta event
options.B: Numeric values are not allowed in state; store the total as a string instead
options.C: Agent Platform sessions expire state keys after one hour; renew them periodically
options.D: The key needs the temp: prefix so that the session service persists it

rationale.A: Changes made directly to a retrieved session's state are not persisted by persistent services; updates must flow through append_event, typically via CallbackContext/ToolContext state or EventActions.state_delta.
rationale.B: State accepts serialisable values; the type is not the problem.
rationale.C: The loss is caused by bypassing the event flow, not by a key TTL.
rationale.D: temp: values are explicitly not persistent.

stem: An ADK agent's instruction contains `Answer in {language}.` Some sessions never set `language` and the agent throws an error before responding. The team wants a default behaviour instead of a crash. What should change?

options.A: Rename the placeholder to {temp:language} so it is always initialised
options.B: Remove templating and ask the model to guess the user's language
options.C: Wrap the whole instruction in a try/except inside a before_agent_callback
options.D: Use {language?} so a missing key does not raise an error

rationale.A: The temp: prefix changes scope, not whether a missing key errors.
rationale.B: Loses the explicit preference when it is set.
rationale.C: Heavy workaround for a built-in templating option.
rationale.D: Instruction templating throws when a key is missing; appending ? makes the key optional.

stem: In an ADK pipeline, a research agent's answer must be available to the next agent as `research_notes` in state, without writing custom code to copy it. What is the simplest mechanism?

options.A: Have the next agent re-run the research agent through AgentTool
options.B: Emit a temp:research_notes key from an after_tool_callback
options.C: Store the answer in Memory Bank and fetch it in the next agent
options.D: Set output_key='research_notes' on the research agent

rationale.A: Duplicates work and cost instead of reading the saved output.
rationale.B: The research agent's answer is not a tool result, and temp: keys vanish after the invocation.
rationale.C: Long-term memory is the wrong store for passing data between steps of one invocation.
rationale.D: An agent's output_key automatically saves its response to the named state key.

stem: An ADK operations agent can call `restart_production_service`. The SRE lead wants the agent to pause and obtain an explicit yes/no from the on-call engineer through the chat UI before the tool runs, and resume afterwards, with no custom approval service. What should you use?

options.A: A Cloud Tasks queue that delays each restart by ten minutes
options.B: A before_model_callback that blocks all model calls containing the word restart
options.C: Tool confirmation: require_confirmation on the FunctionTool, which pauses for a yes/no
options.D: An instruction telling the agent to ask the engineer before calling the restart tool

rationale.A: Delay is not approval, and adds the custom service the lead wanted to avoid.
rationale.B: Blocks rather than asks, and does not resume after approval.
rationale.C: ADK tool confirmation lets a FunctionTool pause execution for a yes/no confirmation; ADK emits a confirmation request event to the client.
rationale.D: Advisory; the model can call the tool without asking.

stem: A procurement agent must not only get approval before `create_purchase_order`, but also collect a cost centre code and an approver comment from the human in a structured form before continuing. Which ADK capability fits?

options.A: Advanced confirmation via request_confirmation, with a hint and an expected payload structure
options.B: require_confirmation=True, then parse the cost centre from the engineer's yes/no reply
options.C: A temp: state key that the human edits directly in the database
options.D: A second agent that asks for the cost centre after the purchase order is created

rationale.A: Advanced confirmation uses the ToolContext request confirmation method with a hint explaining what is needed and a payload describing the expected data.
rationale.B: Boolean confirmation does not collect structured data.
rationale.C: Not a supported interaction and bypasses the event flow.
rationale.D: Collects the data after the action instead of before it.

stem: A team starting a new Python ADK 2.0 project needs a workflow with conditional branches, a loop back to an earlier step on validation failure, and a pause for human input that can resume later. A colleague proposes nesting SequentialAgent, LoopAgent and ParallelAgent. What should you recommend?

options.A: A ParallelAgent for all steps, with the model deciding at the end which results to keep
options.B: A graph-based workflow with explicit nodes, conditional edges and human-input nodes
options.C: A single LlmAgent whose instructions describe every branch and loop condition
options.D: Nest the three template agents, because graph workflows are only available in Java

rationale.A: Parallel execution does not express ordered branches, loops or pauses.
rationale.B: In ADK 2.0 for Python and Go, template workflows are superseded by graph-based and dynamic workflows, which support conditional routing and resumable human input.
rationale.C: Makes control flow non-deterministic and hard to test.
rationale.D: Graph workflows are documented for Python, TypeScript and Go.

stem: Auditors ask how an ADK pipeline decides which step runs next. The pipeline is a SequentialAgent with three sub-agents. What is the accurate answer?

options.A: Gemini ranks the sub-agents at runtime by their descriptions
options.B: The first sub-agent's LLM chooses which of the other two agents to call next
options.C: Order varies with load because sub-agents run as parallel threads
options.D: Order is fixed by the workflow definition; no model decides the orchestration

rationale.A: No model ranks steps in template workflows.
rationale.B: That describes LLM-driven transfer, not a SequentialAgent.
rationale.C: That describes ParallelAgent, not SequentialAgent.
rationale.D: Template workflow agents follow predefined logic without consulting an AI model for orchestration, giving deterministic execution.

stem: In an ADK graph workflow, a human-input node asks a reviewer to approve a generated contract. When the reply arrives, the team wants the node's own logic to run again from the top with the reply available, rather than passing the reply straight to the next node. Which setting controls this?

options.A: payload set to the full contract text
options.B: rerunOnResume set to true on the human-input node
options.C: A LoopAgent wrapped around the node with max_iterations=2
options.D: response_schema set to the approval format

rationale.A: payload supplies context for the client to render.
rationale.B: rerunOnResume=true reruns the interrupted node from the top; the default false routes the reply to successor nodes.
rationale.C: Template loops do not control how a graph node resumes.
rationale.D: response_schema defines the expected reply shape, not resume behaviour.

stem: A bank standardises on ADK but some teams must use a model served outside Google Cloud for contractual reasons, while others use Gemini. The architect wants one framework and one set of patterns. Is ADK a valid choice?

options.A: Only for Java: the Python ADK is limited to Gemini models
options.B: Only through Agent Designer, which exports agents to ADK
options.C: Yes: ADK is open source and model-agnostic
options.D: No: ADK only runs Gemini models on Agent Runtime

rationale.A: Model-agnosticism is not limited to one language.
rationale.B: Unrelated; ADK is used directly in code.
rationale.C: ADK is an open-source, code-first, model-agnostic framework, so one framework can serve teams using different models.
rationale.D: ADK runs locally and on several targets and is model-agnostic.

stem: A wellness coaching agent should remember, weeks later, that a user is vegetarian and training for a half-marathon, but should not replay entire old conversations into every prompt. Conversations are already stored with Agent Platform Sessions. What should you add?

options.A: Memory Bank: generate memories from sessions, then retrieve them by similarity per user
options.B: A larger context window, appending all of the user's past sessions to every request
options.C: A Memorystore for Redis cache keyed by user ID holding the last conversation
options.D: An unprefixed session-state key that stores the user's diet and goals

rationale.A: Memory Bank extracts and consolidates meaningful facts from sessions and retrieves them with similarity search scoped to the user.
rationale.B: Expensive, slow, and eventually exceeds any context limit.
rationale.C: Caches raw recent text rather than extracted, consolidated long-term facts.
rationale.D: Unprefixed state is scoped to one session and is lost in the next.

stem: A user told a travel agent in March 'I live in Lisbon' and in August 'I just moved to Porto'. With Memory Bank, the team sees a single up-to-date memory about the user's city rather than two conflicting facts. Which capability explains this?

options.A: Similarity search returns only the most recent of any two similar memories
options.B: Consolidation merges new facts with existing memories, keeping revisions of the change
options.C: The session service overwrote the March session when the August one was created
options.D: TTL expiry deleted the March memory automatically after 90 days

rationale.A: Retrieval ranks memories; it does not merge or update them.
rationale.B: Memory Bank performs memory consolidation to merge newly extracted information with existing memories and maintains memory revisions.
rationale.C: Sessions are separate conversations; memories are consolidated in Memory Bank.
rationale.D: TTL removes stale memories by time, not by contradiction, and none was configured here.

stem: A B2B SaaS company runs two different agents (billing and onboarding) for thousands of users. Each agent must only retrieve memories created for the same user by that same agent. How should memories be scoped?

options.A: Scope memories by both the user and the agent name
options.B: Use one global scope and add the user ID as a tag in each memory's text
options.C: Create a separate Google Cloud project for each user's memories
options.D: Scope memories by user only and filter by agent in the prompt

rationale.A: Memory Bank isolates collections of memories by identity scope, including agent_name and user fields.
rationale.B: No isolation; one user's memories could surface for another.
rationale.C: Operationally absurd at thousands of users; scopes provide isolation.
rationale.D: Retrieves the other agent's memories and relies on the model to ignore them.

stem: A retail assistant stores shopping preferences in Memory Bank. The privacy team requires preferences that have not been refreshed to be deleted automatically after 180 days. What should you configure?

options.A: A memory revision limit of 180 on each user scope
options.B: An instruction telling the agent to ignore memories older than 180 days
options.C: A nightly Cloud Scheduler job that deletes every memory in the collection
options.D: A time to live (TTL) on the memories

rationale.A: Revision tracking is about history of changes, not age-based deletion.
rationale.B: The data is still retained, which is what privacy wants to prevent.
rationale.C: Deletes fresh preferences too, not just stale ones.
rationale.D: Memory Bank supports setting a TTL so stale memories are deleted automatically.

stem: A banking assistant's Memory Bank keeps storing trivia such as 'user said good morning' while missing what matters: savings goals, risk tolerance and preferred contact channel. How should you improve memory quality?

options.A: Increase similarity-search top-k so the important memories surface more often
options.B: Switch from GenerateMemories to storing every user message with CreateMemory
options.C: Customise generation with topics and few-shot examples of what counts as meaningful
options.D: Lower the TTL so trivial memories expire before they accumulate

rationale.A: Retrieval cannot surface memories that were never extracted.
rationale.B: Stores even more trivia and loses extraction.
rationale.C: Memory Bank configuration supports specific topics and few-shot examples to define what information is considered meaningful.
rationale.D: Deletes important memories on the same schedule.

stem: After adding memory generation at the end of each turn, a support agent's responses are several seconds slower because the agent waits for extraction to finish. Users do not need new memories within the same turn. What should you change?

options.A: Use asynchronous memory generation so the agent does not wait for it to complete
options.B: Generate memories only once a year for each user
options.C: Replace Memory Bank with unprefixed session state to avoid extraction latency
options.D: Move generation into a before_model_callback so it runs before the response

rationale.A: Memory Bank supports asynchronous generation so the agent doesn't have to wait for memory generation to complete.
rationale.B: Makes memory useless for recent preferences.
rationale.C: Loses cross-session memory entirely.
rationale.D: Still blocks the response, just earlier.

stem: A user explicitly clicks 'Remember that I am allergic to peanuts' in a food-ordering app. The team wants this stored as a memory immediately and exactly, without waiting for extraction from the conversation. Which Memory Bank operation fits?

options.A: An app:allergy key so every session sees it
options.B: GenerateMemories on the next session, then check the result
options.C: A temp:allergy key set in the current invocation
options.D: CreateMemory, writing the fact directly to Memory Bank

rationale.A: app: state is shared across all users, leaking one user's allergy.
rationale.B: Extraction may paraphrase or delay a safety-critical fact.
rationale.C: temp: state is discarded after the invocation.
rationale.D: CreateMemory lets agents write memories directly, alongside GenerateMemories from conversation history.

stem: A team develops an ADK agent on Cloud Run and wants managed, persistent sessions from Agent Platform without moving the agent's code to Agent Runtime. Is this possible?

options.A: Only by replicating Firestore data into Agent Runtime nightly
options.B: No: managed sessions only work for agents deployed to Agent Runtime
options.C: Yes: create an Agent Runtime instance as a session store
options.D: Only through Memory Bank, since sessions are not exposed separately

rationale.A: Unnecessary; the managed session API is used directly.
rationale.B: An instance can serve as a session store for agents running elsewhere.
rationale.C: The docs describe creating an Agent Runtime instance to use Sessions without deploying agent code.
rationale.D: Sessions and Memory Bank are distinct services.

stem: A high-traffic agent on Cloud Run needs (1) a sub-millisecond cache of tool responses such as exchange rates valid for 60 seconds and (2) durable conversation history that survives instance restarts and can be listed per user. The team prefers managed services. Which pairing is best?

options.A: Memorystore for Redis for both the cache and the durable conversation history
options.B: Memorystore for Redis for the short-lived cache; managed sessions for history
options.C: Cloud Storage objects for the cache, and in-memory session service for history
options.D: BigQuery for the 60-second cache, and container local disk for conversation history

rationale.A: An in-memory cache is the wrong system of record for durable conversation history.
rationale.B: An in-memory store suits short-TTL caching; durable per-user history belongs in a managed session store.
rationale.C: Object storage is not a sub-millisecond cache and in-memory sessions vanish on restart.
rationale.D: Analytical warehouse latency for a hot cache, and local disk is lost with the instance.

stem: A developer asks their coding agent to 'add an evaluation step and deploy this ADK agent to Cloud Run'. With Agents CLI skills installed, the coding agent runs the right Agents CLI commands on its own. What is this way of working called?

options.A: Agent mode, in which the coding assistant executes CLI commands using the skills
options.B: Human mode, because a human typed the original request into the chat
options.C: Playground mode, which runs agents-cli playground for every request
options.D: Registry mode, in which the Skill Registry executes the commands remotely

rationale.A: Agents CLI describes agent mode, where coding assistants execute the CLI commands, and human mode for direct deterministic use.
rationale.B: Human mode means the developer runs the commands directly.
rationale.C: The playground is a local testing UI.
rationale.D: Skill Registry stores skills; it does not execute CLI commands.

stem: A multi-tenant agent stores sessions in Agent Platform Sessions. A security review requires that a support engineer's tooling can only read sessions belonging to the tenant they support. Which control applies at the session layer?

options.A: A tenant field in each session plus an instruction to the engineer's tool
options.B: Model Armor templates that block other tenants' session data
options.C: A separate agent per tenant so sessions never mix in one instance
options.D: IAM Conditions on session access, scoped to the engineer's tenant

rationale.A: Instructions and conventions are not access control.
rationale.B: Model Armor screens prompts and responses, not session read permissions.
rationale.C: Possible but heavy; IAM Conditions address the requirement directly.
rationale.D: Agent Runtime Sessions support controlling access with IAM Conditions.

stem: An agent's quality improves greatly when it sees a few curated examples similar to the current request, but the examples change weekly and there are thousands. The team wants a managed way to store and retrieve relevant examples at run time. Which Agent Runtime feature fits?

options.A: Code Execution sandbox, running a script that picks examples
options.B: Example Store, which retrieves relevant examples at run time
options.C: Session state, loading all examples into app: keys
options.D: Memory Bank, generating one memory per curated example

rationale.A: The sandbox executes code; it is not an example store.
rationale.B: Agent Runtime includes Example Store for storing and retrieving examples to improve agents.
rationale.C: Thousands of examples in state bloat every request.
rationale.D: Memory Bank holds user-scoped memories from conversations, not curated few-shot examples.

stem: A data-analysis agent writes Python to compute statistics over user-uploaded files. The team wants the generated code to run in an isolated, managed sandbox without operating their own execution cluster, and sometimes needs a custom container with extra libraries. What should they use?

options.A: exec() inside the agent's own process, with a denylist of dangerous modules
options.B: Example Store, which executes stored code snippets on request
options.C: Agent Runtime Code Execution, which offers sandboxes and custom containers
options.D: A Cloud Function per analysis, deployed by the agent at run time

rationale.A: Runs untrusted code next to the agent's credentials; denylists are bypassable.
rationale.B: Example Store holds examples; it does not execute code.
rationale.C: Agent Runtime provides sandboxed code execution with shell access and custom containers (BYOC).
rationale.D: Deploying functions dynamically is slow and hard to secure.

stem: A platform team wants developers' coding agents to follow the company's agent-building conventions (project layout, evaluation thresholds, deployment approvals) whenever they use Agents CLI. The guide mentions configuring skills with Agents CLI, including plugins. What should they do?

options.A: Fork Agents CLI and hard-code the conventions into its commands
options.B: Add the conventions to the Agents CLI help text through an environment variable
options.C: Publish the conventions as a Gemini Enterprise chat agent developers can ask
options.D: Package the conventions as skills, distributed as a plugin with the Agents CLI skills

rationale.A: Maintaining a fork is costly and breaks upgrades.
rationale.B: Not a supported customisation mechanism.
rationale.C: Developers' coding agents would not use it automatically.
rationale.D: Skills and plugins are how coding agents receive packaged, reusable know-how alongside Agents CLI.

stem: In an ADK customer-service app, a 'refund policy' specialist should be called like a function by the main agent — the main agent stays in control and uses the specialist's answer — rather than the conversation being handed over to the specialist. Which composition fits?

options.A: Expose the specialist over A2A inside the same process
options.B: Wrap the specialist with AgentTool and give it to the main agent as a tool
options.C: Add the specialist to sub_agents so the model can transfer control to it
options.D: Put both agents in a ParallelAgent and merge their outputs

rationale.A: A2A is for remote, independently deployed agents, not in-process composition.
rationale.B: Using an agent as a tool keeps control with the caller, which receives the result; sub-agent transfer hands the conversation over.
rationale.C: Transfer moves the conversation to the specialist, the opposite of the requirement.
rationale.D: Parallel fan-out runs both unconditionally rather than calling the specialist on demand.

stem: A team needs to record the exact prompt sent to the model and the raw response for every call an ADK agent makes, for offline debugging, without changing agent behaviour. Which callbacks fit?

options.A: before_model_callback and after_model_callback, both returning None
options.B: An after_model_callback that returns the logged LlmResponse
options.C: before_tool_callback and after_tool_callback, returning a dict
options.D: before_agent_callback and after_agent_callback, returning Content

rationale.A: Model callbacks run immediately before and after LLM calls; returning None leaves behaviour unchanged.
rationale.B: Returning a response replaces the model's output rather than observing it.
rationale.C: Tool callbacks wrap tools, and returning a dict changes results.
rationale.D: Agent-level callbacks do not see each model request, and returning Content overrides output.

stem: A European insurer must choose between a proprietary SaaS model and a self-hosted open model for an agent that reads policyholder medical details. Legal has approved the SaaS provider's regional processing and data-use terms. The ML team is two people. Which factor should weigh most?

options.A: The open model's parameter count, since larger models are more secure
options.B: The SaaS model's benchmark rank, since legal approval makes costs irrelevant
options.C: Operational capacity: with legal cleared, a small team favours managed SaaS over self-hosting
options.D: Self-hosting is always required when medical data is involved, regardless of approvals

rationale.A: Size does not determine security.
rationale.B: Cost and operations still matter after legal approval.
rationale.C: Once security and residency constraints are satisfied, the cost and risk of operating models become decisive for a small team.
rationale.D: Not universally true; approved regional processing can satisfy the constraint.

stem: An engineering support agent retrieves the top 20 chunks for each question. Reviewers confirm the correct chunk is almost always among the 20, but the answer often quotes a less relevant chunk that happens to share vocabulary with the question. Which change targets this failure directly?

options.A: Increase top-k from 20 to 100 so the correct chunk is even more likely to be retrieved
options.B: Replace the embedding model with one trained on a different language pair
options.C: Reduce the chunk size so each chunk contains a single sentence of text
options.D: Rerank the retrieved candidates with a cross-encoder style ranking step before prompting

rationale.A: Recall is already fine; more candidates add noise and cost.
rationale.B: Retrieval already finds the chunk; the ranking of candidates is what fails.
rationale.C: Fragmenting text usually hurts both recall and answer quality.
rationale.D: Reranking re-scores retrieved chunks with deeper query-document understanding; the common pattern retrieves N candidates with an embedding model, then reranks.

stem: A policy agent answers questions about a 900-page handbook. For several questions the correct passage is never retrieved at any k, and inspection shows the passage spans a page break where a table's header and its rows were split into different chunks. What is the best first fix?

options.A: Raise the similarity threshold so only strong matches are returned
options.B: Switch the vector database from one backend to another
options.C: Revise chunking so tables stay intact, with overlap that preserves headers
options.D: Add a reranker so the split chunks are scored higher

rationale.A: A stricter threshold returns even fewer relevant chunks.
rationale.B: The storage engine is not what split the table.
rationale.C: If a chunk does not contain the evidence needed to answer, retrieval cannot recover; chunking is the unit of truth.
rationale.D: Reranking cannot repair a chunk that lacks the evidence.

stem: A team new to RAG must explain the pipeline to stakeholders in the order the stages run for RAG Engine. Which sequence is correct?

options.A: Ingestion, indexing, embedding, chunking, generation, retrieval
options.B: Ingestion, chunking, embedding, indexing, retrieval, generation
options.C: Chunking, generation, embedding, retrieval, indexing, ingestion
options.D: Embedding, ingestion, retrieval, chunking, indexing, generation

rationale.A: Chunking precedes embedding, and retrieval precedes generation.
rationale.B: RAG Engine documents data ingestion, transformation, embedding, indexing into a corpus, retrieval and generation in that order.
rationale.C: Generation is the final stage, not the second.
rationale.D: Embedding cannot precede ingesting and chunking the data.

stem: A team wants a managed RAG pipeline over PDFs that currently sit in Cloud Storage and Google Drive, without building ingestion, chunking and embedding themselves. Which statement about RAG Engine is accurate?

options.A: It ingests from local files, Cloud Storage and Google Drive
options.B: It only ingests documents that are already stored in BigQuery tables
options.C: It requires documents to be converted into embeddings before ingestion
options.D: It indexes data in place and never copies content into a corpus

rationale.A: RAG Engine accepts data from different sources, for example local files, Cloud Storage and Google Drive.
rationale.B: BigQuery is not the only supported source.
rationale.C: Embedding is a stage RAG Engine performs, not a precondition.
rationale.D: Indexing creates a corpus that structures the knowledge base.

stem: An architect is choosing the vector database behind RAG Engine. The team has no existing vector infrastructure, wants the fastest path to a working corpus, and may move to a higher-scale backend later. Which statement helps most?

options.A: RAG Engine has no pluggable backend; the corpus is always stored in BigQuery
options.B: Choosing a backend is irreversible once the corpus is created
options.C: RAG Engine only works with Pinecone, so an account must be created first
options.D: Several backends, including a managed default and Vector Search

rationale.A: Corpora are not stored in BigQuery by default.
rationale.B: Backends can be changed by rebuilding the corpus; nothing makes it permanent.
rationale.C: Pinecone is one of several supported backends.
rationale.D: RAG Engine supports RagManagedDb, Agent Platform Vector Search 2.0, Vector Search, Feature Store, Weaviate and Pinecone, so a team can start managed and migrate.

stem: A marketplace wants one system that stores product JSON documents, filters by payload fields such as price and availability, and ranks by vector similarity in the same query, so it can drop the separate metadata database it maintains beside its vector index. What should it use?

options.A: A BigQuery table with an embedding column scanned per query
options.B: Memorystore for Redis with vectors serialised as strings
options.C: Agent Retrieval collections of data objects, filtered by payload and vector together
options.D: Vector Search 1.0 indexes with a Cloud SQL table holding the payload fields

rationale.A: Full scans do not provide approximate nearest neighbour performance.
rationale.B: Not a vector retrieval service for this scale or query shape.
rationale.C: Agent Retrieval stores JSON data objects in collections and filters by vector similarity and payload data in one place, removing the need for auxiliary storage.
rationale.D: That is exactly the auxiliary-store architecture the team wants to remove.

stem: A team has no ML engineers and wants to avoid running an embedding pipeline, but still needs semantic search over new documents as they arrive in their retrieval collection. Which Agent Retrieval capability helps?

options.A: Autogenerated embeddings from built-in models
options.B: Scheduled exports to Feature Store that generate vectors nightly
options.C: Bring your own embeddings, which is the only supported option
options.D: Automatic chunking of documents into sentences before storage

rationale.A: Agent Retrieval can automatically populate embedding fields using built-in models, and also supports bring-your-own embeddings.
rationale.B: Not how embeddings are produced for a collection, and it is not near-real-time.
rationale.C: BYOE is supported but not the only option.
rationale.D: Chunking strategy is not the described feature.

stem: Two teams use Agent Retrieval. Team A runs a small internal knowledge base with sporadic queries and wants to pay only for what it uses. Team B serves a latency-sensitive consumer feature with steady high QPS and wants predictable, tuned performance. What should each choose?

options.A: Team A resource-based, Team B usage-based, to smooth each team's bill
options.B: Team A usage-based pricing; Team B resource-based pricing for tuned performance
options.C: Neither: Agent Retrieval has a single flat price per collection
options.D: Both teams should use resource-based pricing for consistency across the organisation

rationale.A: Inverts the models: steady high QPS is what resource-based pricing suits.
rationale.B: Agent Retrieval offers usage-based pricing for smaller workloads and resource-based pricing for tuned performance.
rationale.C: Two pricing models are documented.
rationale.D: Team A would pay for provisioned resources it rarely uses.

stem: During design review, an architect says 'we will use Vector Search' and another says 'you mean Agent Retrieval'. For the exam, which statement is accurate?

options.A: Vector Search 1.0 was renamed RAG Engine
options.B: Agent Retrieval evolved from Vector Search 2.0; 1.0 is the ANN index
options.C: Agent Retrieval replaced Agent Search, which no longer exists
options.D: Vector Search 1.0 and Agent Retrieval are two names for the same current product

rationale.A: RAG Engine is a managed RAG pipeline service, not a renamed index.
rationale.B: Vector Search 1.0 is the ANN index-as-a-service product; Agent Retrieval shifts to collections and data objects while keeping that performance.
rationale.C: Agent Search (formerly Vertex AI Search) is a separate enterprise search product.
rationale.D: They are distinct: 1.0 is index-centric, Agent Retrieval is collection-centric.

stem: After a quarterly refresh of the knowledge base, a RAG agent's answers get worse although tool calls and prompts are unchanged. The team wants to detect this class of regression automatically in future. What should they add? (Choose two.)

options.A: A retrieval evaluation that scores whether the right documents are returned for golden queries
options.B: A latency alert on the retrieval service
options.C: A scheduled evaluation run against the golden dataset after every corpus refresh
options.D: A rule that forbids corpus refreshes without a change-advisory board
options.E: A larger top-k at query time to compensate for future corpus changes

rationale.A: Retrieval quality must be measured separately from answer quality to catch corpus regressions.
rationale.B: Latency did not change; relevance did.
rationale.C: Running the evaluation on each refresh turns the check into a gate rather than a post-mortem.
rationale.D: Process friction that still provides no evidence about quality.
rationale.E: Masks the problem and adds noise instead of detecting it.

stem: A retrieval system for a multilingual support centre returns good results in English but poor results for Portuguese and Japanese questions over the same translated documents. Chunking and reranking are already in place. What is the most likely cause?

options.A: Top-k is set too low for non-English questions specifically
options.B: The vector index uses cosine similarity instead of dot product
options.C: The corpus needs to be re-indexed once per language into separate backends
options.D: The embedding model does not handle those languages well

rationale.A: A global k does not discriminate by language.
rationale.B: The distance metric does not explain a per-language gap.
rationale.C: Separate indexes are not required when the embedding model is multilingual.
rationale.D: Retrieval quality across languages depends on the embedding model's multilingual coverage.

stem: Users search a parts catalogue with exact identifiers such as 'MX-4471-B' as well as descriptive phrases like 'waterproof connector for marine use'. Pure vector search often misses the exact part number. What retrieval design handles both?

options.A: Hybrid retrieval of keyword and vector, then reranking
options.B: Keyword-only search, since part numbers are the most common query
options.C: Storing part numbers in the prompt so the model can match them
options.D: Vector-only search with a much larger embedding model

rationale.A: Exact identifiers favour lexical matching while descriptions favour semantics; combining both and reranking serves both query types.
rationale.B: Descriptive queries would then fail.
rationale.C: Does not scale to a catalogue and is not retrieval.
rationale.D: Bigger embeddings still struggle with rare exact tokens.

stem: A compliance agent must answer only from the company's approved corpus and must show which document each statement came from. Which combination of RAG Engine behaviour supports this?

options.A: Indexing rewrites the corpus into the model's weights for faithful recall
options.B: Generation uses the model's parametric knowledge and cites the corpus afterwards
options.C: Retrieval supplies relevant context and generation is grounded in it, with sources kept
options.D: Retrieval returns whole documents so the model can quote any part of them

rationale.A: Indexing builds a searchable corpus; it does not train the model.
rationale.B: Citing sources not used to produce the answer is misleading.
rationale.C: RAG Engine retrieves relevant knowledge and uses it as a guide for factually grounded responses, which is what makes citation possible.
rationale.D: Whole-document context is not required and often exceeds limits.

stem: A collection in Agent Retrieval holds documents with two vector fields: one for the title and one for the body. The team needs fast approximate search on both. What does the service support?

options.A: A single index per collection, so the fields must be merged into one vector
options.B: Indexes only on payload fields, with vectors always scanned exhaustively
options.C: One collection per vector field, joined at query time by the client
options.D: Multiple collection indexes, for example one per vector field

rationale.A: Multiple indexes per collection are supported.
rationale.B: Indexes exist precisely for ANN vector search.
rationale.C: Unnecessary duplication of the data.
rationale.D: Collections support multiple indexes, such as one per vector field, to enable efficient ANN search.

stem: A pricing agent answers from a RAG corpus rebuilt nightly. Sales reports that prices quoted during the day are stale after mid-morning promotions. Rebuilding the whole corpus hourly is too expensive. What is the best design change?

options.A: Tell users in the system prompt that prices may be out of date
options.B: Fetch live prices with a tool at answer time
options.C: Increase the corpus rebuild frequency to every 15 minutes
options.D: Cache yesterday's answers and serve them faster

rationale.A: A disclaimer does not fix wrong quotes.
rationale.B: Volatile facts belong behind a tool call; retrieval corpora suit slow-changing knowledge.
rationale.C: Expensive and still stale between rebuilds.
rationale.D: Serves stale prices more quickly.

stem: A RAG agent retrieves six good chunks but its answers frequently ignore two of them and contradict a third. The chunks are concatenated into the prompt without structure. What should the team try first?

options.A: Add document delimiters, titles and citation instructions
options.B: Switch to a model with a larger context window
options.C: Lower the temperature to zero so the model reads more carefully
options.D: Remove three of the six chunks at random to reduce context size

rationale.A: Well-delimited, labelled context with explicit grounding instructions improves how reliably the model uses retrieved passages.
rationale.B: The problem is prompt structure, not capacity.
rationale.C: Sampling temperature does not make a model attend to ignored passages.
rationale.D: Arbitrary removal may drop the needed evidence.

stem: An organisation wants employees to ask questions across Drive, SharePoint and Jira with per-user permissions honoured, and does not want to build a retrieval pipeline. A developer proposes writing a custom RAG Engine corpus over exports of these systems. What is the better choice and why?

options.A: Agent Retrieval, because collections enforce per-user access automatically
options.B: A BigQuery export with row-level security applied to each document
options.C: Agent Search with connectors, because it preserves per-user document permissions
options.D: RAG Engine, because it is the only service that supports third-party sources

rationale.A: Agent Retrieval is a vector store; it does not implement enterprise document ACLs.
rationale.B: Rebuilds search and permissions from scratch for a solved problem.
rationale.C: Agent Search data stores carry ACLs and use the identity provider to filter results per user, which exports into a custom corpus would lose.
rationale.D: Agent Search connectors cover third-party sources including SharePoint and Jira.

stem: A team in Singapore plans a production launch on RAG Engine and asks whether they can rely on the same launch stage as their colleagues in us-central1. What is the correct guidance?

options.A: Region choice only affects latency, never feature availability
options.B: Check the launch stage per region, since availability differs between regions
options.C: Preview regions carry the same SLA as GA regions
options.D: Launch stages are global, so any region behaves the same as us-central1

rationale.A: Feature and launch-stage differences are documented by region.
rationale.B: RAG Engine documents different launch stages by region, including allowlist GA, GA and preview regions.
rationale.C: Preview features do not carry GA service levels.
rationale.D: The documentation lists different stages per region.

stem: A RAG agent sends 18 retrieved chunks of 1,500 tokens each into every request, and cost is dominated by input tokens. Evaluation shows answer quality is unchanged when only the top 5 chunks are used. What should the team do?

options.A: Cache the 18 chunks per query string for an hour
options.B: Summarise each chunk with a second model call before the main call
options.C: Retrieve broadly but rerank and pass only the top chunks to the model
options.D: Keep all 18 chunks but switch to a cheaper model to halve the price

rationale.A: Caching identical queries does not reduce per-request context.
rationale.B: Adds calls and latency to fix a problem reranking solves.
rationale.C: Reranking lets the system keep recall while cutting the tokens sent to the model, with quality verified by evaluation.
rationale.D: Reduces quality while still paying for unnecessary context.

stem: A team wants some fields in their Agent Retrieval collection to be validated strictly while allowing additional ad-hoc fields on some documents during a migration. What does the service offer?

options.A: Schema definitions supporting both strict and relaxed validation
options.B: Strict validation only, so all documents must match one schema
options.C: Schema enforcement only on vector fields, never on payload fields
options.D: No schema support; every document is an opaque blob

rationale.A: Data objects in collections have schema definitions supporting strict and relaxed validation.
rationale.B: Relaxed validation is supported.
rationale.C: Validation covers the data object's fields generally.
rationale.D: Collections define schemas over JSON data objects.

stem: During a design review, a junior engineer proposes storing raw text in the vector field and computing similarity with string edit distance to 'avoid the cost of embeddings'. Why is this wrong for semantic retrieval?

options.A: Vector fields reject text values, so the design cannot be implemented
options.B: Edit distance is too slow to compute for any corpus larger than a few documents
options.C: Edit distance requires a GPU, making it more expensive than embeddings
options.D: Edit distance compares characters, so paraphrases with no shared words score as unrelated

rationale.A: The conceptual flaw matters more than a field-type error.
rationale.B: Speed is not the core issue; semantics are.
rationale.C: It is cheap to compute; it is simply the wrong measure.
rationale.D: Semantic retrieval relies on embeddings that place similar meanings close together, which lexical distance cannot do.

stem: Twelve agents in one project share a service account. Auditors cannot tell which agent performed an action, and a developer once created a long-lived key for that account. The team wants per-agent principals with no downloadable keys. What should they adopt?

options.A: One service account per agent, with keys stored in Secret Manager
options.B: Workload Identity Federation from an external identity provider per agent
options.C: A single service account with IAM Conditions per agent name
options.D: Agent Identity, giving each agent its own non-impersonable principal

rationale.A: Still key-based and impersonable; it only multiplies the accounts.
rationale.B: Federation maps external identities; Agent Identity is the platform's native per-agent principal.
rationale.C: Conditions cannot distinguish agents that share one identity.
rationale.D: Agent identities are not shared by default, cannot be impersonated, and do not allow long-lived key generation, unlike service accounts.

stem: An architect must write an IAM policy that grants a specific agent access to a Cloud Storage bucket. The agent's identity is shown in documentation as a SPIFFE ID. What must they do in the policy?

options.A: Use the identity with the principal:// prefix as the member in the binding
options.B: Grant the role to allAuthenticatedUsers and filter by an IAM Condition on the agent name
options.C: Use the spiffe:// identifier exactly as displayed
options.D: Reference the underlying service account email instead

rationale.A: Agent identities follow the SPIFFE format, and in IAM policies the identifier uses principal:// instead of spiffe://.
rationale.B: Far too broad and not how agent principals are referenced.
rationale.C: IAM policies use the principal:// form of the identifier.
rationale.D: Agent identities are distinct principals, not service-account emails.

stem: A security reviewer asks how an agent using Agent Identity proves who it is when calling Google Cloud APIs, and how the credential is rotated. What is the accurate answer?

options.A: A static API key stored in Secret Manager and rotated every 90 days
options.B: An OAuth refresh token per agent, refreshed by the developer
options.C: X.509 certificates auto-provisioned with 24-hour validity, used with mTLS
options.D: A service-account key JSON file mounted into the agent container

rationale.A: Agent Identity does not rely on static API keys for this.
rationale.B: Not the mechanism for agent-to-Google Cloud authentication.
rationale.C: Agent Identity auto-provisions and manages X.509 certificates valid for 24 hours and uses mutual TLS with Google Cloud APIs.
rationale.D: Agent identities explicitly avoid long-lived keys.

stem: A team grants an agent identity access to a legacy bucket by adding `roles/storage.legacyBucketReader`, and the grant fails. What is the explanation?

options.A: Legacy roles require the agent to be in the same project as the bucket
options.B: Agent identities cannot be granted legacy bucket roles; use a supported role
options.C: The bucket must have uniform bucket-level access disabled first
options.D: Legacy roles can only be granted to groups, not to individual principals

rationale.A: Project location is not the documented limitation.
rationale.B: The documentation states agent identities cannot be granted legacy bucket roles such as storage.legacyBucketReader.
rationale.C: That is unrelated to the agent-identity restriction.
rationale.D: The restriction is specific to agent identities.

stem: An agent must read a user's calendar in a third-party SaaS product on that user's behalf. The security team requires that the agent code never sees the user's OAuth token, and nobody wants to implement the consent and refresh flow. What should you use?

options.A: 2-legged OAuth with the agent's own credentials for all users
options.B: Agent Identity auth manager with a 3-legged OAuth provider for user consent
options.C: A service account with domain-wide delegation impersonating each user
options.D: Prompting the user to paste an access token into the chat

rationale.A: Machine-to-machine auth cannot act on behalf of a specific user with consent.
rationale.B: The auth manager handles OAuth flows including user consent and token refresh, stores tokens in a Google-managed vault, and with Agent Gateway the agent never sees the raw credential.
rationale.C: Bypasses user consent and grants broad standing access.
rationale.D: Puts a live credential into conversation history.

stem: An agent calls a weather API that authenticates with an API key, and a partner API that uses machine-to-machine OAuth. The team wants both credentials handled outside agent code and injected into tool calls. Which statement is correct?

options.A: API keys must be embedded in the MCP server configuration file
options.B: Both credentials must be fetched from Secret Manager by the agent at start-up
options.C: The auth manager handles only 3-legged OAuth; API keys must stay in code
options.D: The auth manager supports API keys and 2-legged OAuth, injecting headers into tool calls

rationale.A: That spreads secrets into configuration instead of the vault.
rationale.B: Possible generally, but it is not the managed pattern described.
rationale.C: API keys are explicitly supported.
rationale.D: Agent Identity auth manager supports 3-legged OAuth, 2-legged OAuth and API keys, and integrates with ADK to inject outbound auth headers into tool and MCP invocations.

stem: A 400-engineer organisation keeps rebuilding the same capabilities because teams cannot find existing agents, skills and MCP tools. Leadership wants one catalog to discover and reuse them, with governance applied centrally. What should they adopt?

options.A: Example Store, which holds reusable agent examples for discovery
options.B: Model Garden, extended with the organisation's internal agents
options.C: Agent Registry as the central catalog
options.D: A Confluence page per team listing their agents and tools

rationale.A: Example Store serves few-shot examples at run time.
rationale.B: Model Garden catalogs foundation models.
rationale.C: Agent Registry is a centralized catalog to store, discover and govern MCP servers, tools, standalone skills and agents.
rationale.D: Documentation drifts and provides no governance or programmatic discovery.

stem: A partner runs an A2A agent on their own infrastructure. Your company's orchestrator must discover and call it under the same governance as internal agents. What is required?

options.A: Register the external agent manually in Agent Registry
options.B: Add the partner's URL to the orchestrator's prompt as a rule
options.C: Nothing: Agent Registry discovers any A2A agent reachable on the internet
