options.D: Ask the partner to deploy their agent to your Agent Runtime instance

rationale.A: Agents deployed on Agent Runtime register automatically; external or third-party endpoints must be registered explicitly.
rationale.B: No governance, no discovery, no policy enforcement.
rationale.C: There is no automatic discovery of external endpoints.
rationale.D: Unnecessary and usually impossible for a partner-operated agent.

stem: After deploying several A2A-capable agents to Agent Runtime, a team wants to know what appears in Agent Registry without extra work. What happens automatically?

options.A: Only the agent names appear; skills must be typed in by hand
options.B: They register and their A2A skills are extracted
options.C: The agents' source repositories are indexed for discovery
options.D: Nothing is registered until an administrator approves each agent

rationale.A: Skills are extracted as part of automatic registration.
rationale.B: Automatic registration from Agent Runtime records the agents and extracts A2A skills into Agent Registry.
rationale.C: Registry catalogs endpoints and capabilities, not source code.
rationale.D: Registration from Agent Runtime is automatic.

stem: Security wants a single place to declare which external APIs and services agents may reach, so that gateway policy can be applied consistently instead of each team hard-coding URLs. Which Agent Registry capability addresses this?

options.A: Storing allowed URLs in each agent's system instructions
options.B: Creating a firewall rule per destination in the agents' VPC
options.C: Registering endpoints as target destinations for central governance
options.D: Registering each team's source repository as a governed resource

rationale.A: Instructions are not enforcement and are not central.
rationale.B: Network rules cannot express agent-level policy or tool semantics.
rationale.C: Agent Registry lets you register endpoints to define target destinations, centrally governing the external APIs and services agents can connect to.
rationale.D: Repositories are not the runtime destinations policy applies to.

stem: An agent must query an operational AlloyDB database and a Firestore collection as part of answering customer questions. The team wants Google-managed tool endpoints rather than maintaining servers. What is available?

options.A: Only BigQuery has a managed MCP server; other databases need custom servers
options.B: Managed MCP servers exist but cannot be used by ADK agents, only by coding agents
options.C: Database access from agents must always go through a custom integration layer
options.D: Managed MCP servers for Google Cloud databases including AlloyDB and Firestore

rationale.A: Managed servers exist for several database services.
rationale.B: They are MCP endpoints usable by agents generally.
rationale.C: Managed MCP servers are the prebuilt option.
rationale.D: Google Cloud offers managed MCP servers for AlloyDB, Spanner, Cloud SQL, Firestore and Bigtable.

stem: A retailer's agent needs to place orders in a proprietary ERP that exposes a SOAP API with unusual error semantics, and the team wants the capability reusable by several agents with one place to fix bugs. What is the best approach?

options.A: Build a custom MCP server wrapping the ERP, and register it for reuse
options.B: Export ERP data nightly so agents can read files instead of ordering
options.C: Give each agent an HTTP tool that posts raw SOAP envelopes to the ERP
options.D: Add the ERP's WSDL to each agent's system instructions

rationale.A: A custom MCP server creates a reusable integration layer for APIs that have no prebuilt tool, and registration makes it discoverable and governable.
rationale.B: Reading exports cannot place orders.
rationale.C: Duplicates parsing and error handling in every agent.
rationale.D: Instructions do not perform calls or handle errors.

stem: A governance team asks what evidence exists when an agent queries BigQuery through the managed remote MCP server. What can you tell them?

options.A: Evidence requires enabling a separate MCP audit feature per agent
options.B: Queries are anonymous because MCP servers do not carry identity
options.C: Calls are authorised with IAM and recorded in audit logging
options.D: Only the agent's own application logs record the queries

rationale.A: Audit logging is part of the managed service.
rationale.B: The managed server authorises with IAM.
rationale.C: The BigQuery remote MCP server runs on managed infrastructure with HTTPS endpoints, IAM authorization and audit logging.
rationale.D: Audit logging is provided by the managed service.

stem: An agent needs to read one Cloud Storage prefix and write to one Pub/Sub topic. A developer proposes granting the agent identity Editor on the project 'so it does not break later'. What should the reviewer require instead?

options.A: A shared service account with Editor, used by all agents for simplicity
options.B: Editor now, with a scheduled review to reduce permissions next quarter
options.C: Editor on a dedicated project containing only these two resources
options.D: Narrow bindings on that bucket prefix and topic

rationale.A: Reintroduces shared identities and broad access.
rationale.B: Leaves excessive access in production indefinitely in practice.
rationale.C: Still grants broad rights, including on future resources in that project.
rationale.D: Per-agent identities exist so permissions can be granted narrowly and audited per agent.

stem: An MCP server exposes one tool called `run_sql` that accepts arbitrary SQL against the production database. Reviewers worry the agent will run destructive statements. Which redesign best reduces risk while keeping the agent useful?

options.A: Keep run_sql but require the agent to explain each query before running it
options.B: Expose narrow, purpose-built tools with parameters, backed by least-privilege IAM
options.C: Keep run_sql but instruct the agent to only write SELECT statements
options.D: Keep run_sql and add a regex filter for DROP and DELETE keywords

rationale.A: An explanation does not prevent execution.
rationale.B: Purpose-built tools constrain what the agent can express, and least-privilege credentials bound the damage.
rationale.C: Instructions do not constrain generated SQL.
rationale.D: Keyword filters are easy to evade and miss dangerous updates.

stem: A team runs one agent on Agent Runtime and another in a container on Cloud Run, and wants both to use Agent Identity rather than shared service accounts. Is that supported?

options.A: Yes: Agent Identity supports Agent Runtime, Gemini Enterprise and Cloud Run
options.B: No: Agent Identity is only available for agents deployed to Agent Runtime
options.C: Only with Anthos Service Mesh issuing the certificates
options.D: Only if the Cloud Run agent is rewritten with ADK

rationale.A: The documentation lists Agent Runtime, Gemini Enterprise and Cloud Run as supported runtimes for Agent Identity.
rationale.B: Cloud Run and Gemini Enterprise are listed as supported.
rationale.C: Certificates are auto-provisioned by the platform.
rationale.D: Framework choice is not the gating factor.

stem: Different teams have registered MCP servers whose tools overlap, and an orchestrator must choose reliable ones. Which Agent Registry capability helps the orchestrator use standardised integration?

options.A: Ranking tools by popularity so the orchestrator always picks the most used
options.B: Locating endpoints through standardised MCP or A2A
options.C: Executing tools on behalf of agents so orchestrators need no clients
options.D: Automatically merging duplicate tools into one canonical entry

rationale.A: Not a described capability.
rationale.B: Agent Registry lets you use standardized MCP or A2A protocols to locate and connect to functional endpoints, reducing infrastructure overhead.
rationale.C: Registry is a catalog; execution happens at the endpoints.
rationale.D: The registry catalogs entries; it does not merge tools for you.

stem: An insurance quote agent must gather a credit score, a claims history and a vehicle valuation from three independent services. Each call takes about two seconds and none depends on the others. Today they run one after another and users wait six seconds. What orchestration should you use?

options.A: A sequential chain, ordered so the fastest service is called first to improve perceived latency
options.B: A single LLM call whose prompt asks the model to fetch all three data points at once
options.C: A loop that retries all three services until each returns within two seconds
options.D: A parallel step that fans out the three calls, then a sequential step that combines them

rationale.A: Ordering does not reduce total wall-clock time for independent calls.
rationale.B: The model still issues tool calls, and prompting does not guarantee concurrency.
rationale.C: Loops repeat work; they do not run independent calls concurrently.
rationale.D: Independent subtasks belong in parallel execution; the dependent aggregation step follows sequentially.

stem: A content pipeline must draft an article, then fact-check the draft, then rewrite it using the fact-check findings. Each step needs the previous step's output, and the team wants deterministic order with no model deciding the sequence. What fits best?

options.A: A SequentialAgent whose sub-agents pass results through state with output_key
options.B: Three separate agents called by the user in turn from the chat interface
options.C: A ParallelAgent so drafting and fact-checking start together and reconcile at the end
options.D: An LlmAgent with three tools, letting the model decide when each runs

rationale.A: Template workflow agents run sub-agents in a fixed order without a model orchestrating, and output_key carries each result forward in session state.
rationale.B: Pushes orchestration onto the user and loses automation.
rationale.C: Fact-checking depends on the draft, so parallel execution has nothing to check.
rationale.D: Introduces non-determinism the team explicitly does not want.

stem: A code-generation agent should keep improving its output until a validator passes, but must stop after a bounded number of attempts to avoid runaway cost. Which template workflow agent expresses this?

options.A: A ParallelAgent running ten generation attempts and picking the best
options.B: An LlmAgent instructed to try again until the validator is happy
options.C: A LoopAgent that repeats its sub-agents until a termination condition is met
options.D: A SequentialAgent listing the generator and validator twice

rationale.A: Pays for ten attempts every time regardless of the first result.
rationale.B: Unbounded and non-deterministic, which is the risk being avoided.
rationale.C: LoopAgent repeatedly executes its sub-agents until a specific termination condition is met, which bounds iteration.
rationale.D: Fixes the attempts at two and does not express a stop condition.

stem: A team converts a sequential ADK pipeline into a ParallelAgent so three sub-agents run at once. Each sub-agent writes its findings to the same state key. Results are now inconsistent between runs. What is the cause and fix?

options.A: Parallel execution is non-deterministic by design, so revert to sequential execution
options.B: Parallel branches share state, so give each sub-agent a distinct output_key
options.C: The session service cannot handle concurrent writes, so switch to in-memory sessions
options.D: A LoopAgent must wrap the ParallelAgent to serialise the writes

rationale.A: Parallel execution is fine here; the collision is caused by the shared key.
rationale.B: Parallel sub-agents execute concurrently against shared session state, so writes to one key collide; distinct keys keep results separate.
rationale.C: Changing session backend does not resolve two writers using one key.
rationale.D: Loops repeat the work rather than separating outputs.

stem: Your company's ADK claims agent must delegate part of a workflow to a partner's agent, which is built on a different framework and runs on the partner's own infrastructure. Its internal tools and memory must stay private. Which protocol fits?

options.A: MCP, exposing the partner's tools directly to your agent
options.B: A shared session store so both agents read and write the same conversation state
options.C: A2A, where the remote agent stays opaque and receives tasks
options.D: A nightly batch file exchange between the two companies

rationale.A: MCP connects an agent to tools and servers; it would require exposing their internals.
rationale.B: Couples the systems and violates the privacy requirement.
rationale.C: A2A is agent-to-agent: the remote agent exposes an HTTP endpoint and its internal workings, memory and tools are not exposed to the client.
rationale.D: Not interactive delegation and far too slow for a workflow step.

stem: Before calling a remote A2A agent, your orchestrator must learn what that agent can do, where to send requests and how to authenticate. Which A2A concept provides this?

options.A: The Part, which declares the supported content types for the agent
options.B: The Task object, which carries capability metadata on first contact
options.C: The Artifact, which the remote agent returns describing itself
options.D: The Agent Card, the remote agent's discovery document

rationale.A: A Part is the content container inside messages and artifacts.
rationale.B: A Task is a stateful unit of work, not a discovery document.
rationale.C: Artifacts are outputs generated during a task.
rationale.D: The Agent Card serves as a digital business card for discovery and interaction setup, listing endpoints, capabilities, authentication requirements and skills.

stem: An A2A remote agent needs more information from the user halfway through a long-running job, and your client must react to that. Which A2A element models this interaction?

options.A: The Task, whose lifecycle can require input
options.B: An Artifact containing a form the client must render
options.C: The Agent Card, refreshed to advertise the required input
options.D: A Message with the role set to system, which pauses the task

rationale.A: A Task is a stateful unit of work with a unique ID and defined lifecycle, which is how a remote agent signals that it needs input.
rationale.B: Artifacts are outputs; task state signals the need for input.
rationale.C: The card is discovery metadata, not per-task state.
rationale.D: Messages are turns of communication, not lifecycle control.

stem: A research agent delegates a five-minute literature review to a remote A2A agent. The user interface should show partial results as they appear rather than waiting. Which A2A interaction pattern fits?

options.A: Push notifications to a webhook, which the browser receives directly
options.B: Request/response polling every 30 seconds until completion
options.C: Streaming with server-sent events for incremental results
options.D: Opening one WebSocket per artifact produced by the remote agent

rationale.A: Push notifications target server-side webhooks, not the user's browser session.
rationale.B: Polling is supported but shows nothing between polls and adds latency.
rationale.C: A2A supports streaming with SSE so clients receive real-time, incremental results.
rationale.D: Not the documented A2A transport pattern.

stem: A document-processing agent delegates a job that can take hours to a remote A2A agent. Your client should not hold a connection open, and the system must be notified when the work completes. Which A2A mechanism fits?

options.A: Server-sent events held open for the duration of the job
options.B: Polling the Agent Card until its status field changes
options.C: Synchronous request/response with a long timeout
options.D: Push notifications to a client webhook when the task updates

rationale.A: Keeping a stream open for hours is fragile and was explicitly excluded.
rationale.B: Agent Cards describe capabilities; they do not carry task status.
rationale.C: Ties up the client and often exceeds gateway timeouts.
rationale.D: A2A push notifications let the server send asynchronous updates to client webhooks, which suits long-running work.

stem: A platform team is writing integration tests that post directly to a partner's A2A endpoint instead of using an SDK, so the tests must construct the request bodies by hand. Before writing the fixtures they must confirm the transport and payload format A2A uses. What is it?

options.A: GraphQL queries over HTTPS
options.B: JSON-RPC 2.0 payloads over HTTP(S)
options.C: gRPC with protobuf messages over HTTP/2
options.D: SOAP envelopes over HTTP with WS-Security

rationale.A: A2A does not use GraphQL.
rationale.B: A2A communication occurs over HTTP(S) with JSON-RPC 2.0 as the payload format.
rationale.C: Not the documented A2A payload format.
rationale.D: Not part of the A2A specification.

stem: Match the protocol to the integration: (1) your agent must call your company's inventory database through a server that exposes query tools, and (2) your agent must hand a fulfilment task to a logistics partner's autonomous agent. Which pairing is correct?

options.A: (1) MCP for the tool server; (2) A2A for the partner agent
options.B: A2A for both, since every integration can be modelled as an agent
options.C: (1) A2A for the database server; (2) MCP for the partner agent
options.D: MCP for both, since the partner agent can expose itself as a tool server

rationale.A: MCP connects agents to tools and servers, while A2A handles agent-to-agent delegation across organisations and frameworks.
rationale.B: A database tool server is not an autonomous agent.
rationale.C: Inverts the two protocols' purposes.
rationale.D: Possible in theory, but it discards A2A's task lifecycle and opacity model.

stem: A team deploys three A2A agents to Agent Runtime and expects to spend a sprint wiring them into the organisation's catalog and gateway policy. What actually happens, and what is left to do?

options.A: Nothing is automatic: registration, gateway routing and policy all require manual setup
options.B: They register automatically and route through the gateway; policy still needs authoring
options.C: Everything is automatic, including a default deny-all authorization policy
options.D: Registration is automatic only after the first successful A2A call from another agent

rationale.A: Registration and gateway routing are automatic for Agent Runtime.
rationale.B: Agents on Agent Runtime register in Agent Registry automatically and their traffic goes through Agent Gateway, but authorization policies must still be configured.
rationale.C: Policies are authored by the team; they are not created for you.
rationale.D: Registration happens on deployment, not on first call.

stem: An agent on Agent Runtime in project A must call a tool service in project B. The platform team wants the call governed centrally. What is required?

options.A: Grant the agent identity the Editor role in project B
options.B: Peer the two VPCs and allow the traffic with firewall rules
options.C: Enable Client-to-Agent ingress mode in project B for the incoming call
options.D: Register the destination and use Agent-to-Anywhere egress

rationale.A: Over-broad and still bypasses central policy.
rationale.B: Network connectivity is not agent-level governance.
rationale.C: Ingress mode governs clients calling agents, not an agent's outbound call.
rationale.D: Cross-project destinations are registered in the gateway project and are governed through the Agent-to-Anywhere egress path.

stem: A platform team plans to register every internal API as a governed destination behind one Agent Gateway instance. They estimate 7,000 resources. What should they know?

options.A: There is no limit, but latency grows linearly with the number of resources
options.B: Only MCP servers count toward the limit, so APIs can be added freely
options.C: A gateway instance supports at most 5,000 registered resources
options.D: Registered resources are limited to 500 per project across all gateways

rationale.A: A documented maximum exists.
rationale.B: The limit applies to registered resources generally.
rationale.C: Agent Gateway documents a maximum of 5,000 registered resources per gateway instance.
rationale.D: Not the documented limit.

stem: A team wants to route an agent's connection to a legacy system that speaks a custom TCP protocol through Agent Gateway, and the destination uses a self-signed certificate. What is the correct assessment?

options.A: Unsupported: the gateway handles HTTP traffic and rejects self-signed certificates
options.B: Supported if the self-signed certificate is uploaded to the gateway's trust store
options.C: Supported only in Client-to-Agent mode, which does not inspect certificates
options.D: Supported once the custom protocol is wrapped in gRPC with the certificate pinned

rationale.A: Agent Gateway does not support non-HTTP protocols and cannot connect to destinations with self-signed certificates.
rationale.B: The documented limitation excludes self-signed certificate destinations.
rationale.C: Neither mode removes these limitations.
rationale.D: Non-HTTP protocols remain unsupported.

stem: A bank wants a rule that an agent may never combine 'export customer list' with 'send external email' in the same session, expressed in business language and evaluated before each tool call. Which capability fits?

options.A: A system instruction listing forbidden tool combinations
options.B: Semantic governance policies evaluated at the gateway
options.C: An IAM deny policy on the export tool for the agent's identity
options.D: Model Armor templates configured with the two tool names

rationale.A: Advisory and easily bypassed.
rationale.B: Semantic governance evaluates proposed tool calls against user intent and natural-language constraints at the Agent Gateway, protecting against toxic tool combinations.
rationale.C: Blocks the tool entirely rather than the dangerous combination.
rationale.D: Model Armor screens prompt and response content, not tool-combination policy.

stem: A team is about to enable semantic governance policies in production for the first time and worries about blocking legitimate traffic. What is the recommended rollout?

options.A: Start in dry-run mode to validate the configuration without blocking
options.B: Enable enforcement for 10% of agents chosen at random
options.C: Write the policies but leave them unattached until an incident occurs
options.D: Enable enforcement and roll back if error rates rise

rationale.A: The documentation recommends deploying semantic governance policies in dry-run mode first to validate configuration without blocking traffic.
rationale.B: Partial enforcement still blocks real traffic and gives a partial view.
rationale.C: Provides no validation and no protection.
rationale.D: Causes the outage the team is trying to avoid.

stem: An architect asks whether agents deployed on Agent Runtime can interoperate with agents built on other frameworks through an open protocol. What is accurate?

options.A: Only MCP is supported, so other agents must expose themselves as tool servers
options.B: Interoperability requires all agents to be rewritten in ADK
options.C: Agent Runtime supports the A2A protocol for multi-agent interoperability
options.D: Cross-framework calls must go through Gemini Enterprise

rationale.A: A2A is supported for agent-to-agent interaction.
rationale.B: Runtime supports several frameworks and A2A for cross-framework interoperability.
rationale.C: Agent Runtime lists Agent2Agent (A2A) as a supported open protocol for multi-agent interoperability.
rationale.D: Not a requirement for A2A interoperability.

stem: A claims workflow must branch: simple claims are auto-approved, medium claims go to a review agent, and high-value claims go to a human and then back into the workflow if approved. The team wants the routing logic explicit and testable rather than emergent from a prompt. Which design fits best?

options.A: A ParallelAgent that runs all three paths and discards the irrelevant results
options.B: One LlmAgent with instructions describing the three paths and when to use each
options.C: A SequentialAgent with all three handlers in order and early returns in prompts
options.D: A graph workflow with conditional edges and a human-input node that resumes

rationale.A: Wasteful and would auto-approve claims that need review.
rationale.B: Makes routing emergent and hard to test, the opposite of the requirement.
rationale.C: Sequential templates cannot express branching or a resumable pause.
rationale.D: Graph workflows express conditional routing and resumable human input explicitly, keeping control flow testable.

stem: In a graph workflow, a compliance officer must approve a generated filing before submission, and may respond hours later. What does the human-input node provide?

options.A: A LoopAgent that polls an approvals table every minute
options.B: A pause with a message, payload and response schema that resumes on reply
options.C: An email tool invocation that returns immediately with a default approval
options.D: A blocking model call that keeps asking the officer until they answer

rationale.A: Polling logic is unnecessary; the node resumes on reply.
rationale.B: Human-input nodes pause without invoking a model, carry message, payload and response_schema, and the workflow resumes when the reply arrives.
rationale.C: Defaulting to approval defeats the control.
rationale.D: Human-input nodes do not require a model and do not busy-wait.

stem: A support agent handles billing and technical issues with two specialists. The business wants the conversation to move fully to the specialist once a topic is identified, including follow-up questions, until the user changes topic. Which ADK composition matches?

options.A: A SequentialAgent that always runs billing then technical
options.B: AgentTool wrappers so the root agent calls specialists per question
options.C: Separate deployments called over A2A for each user turn
options.D: Sub-agents with LLM-driven transfer of control between them

rationale.A: Runs both specialists regardless of topic.
rationale.B: Keeps control at the root, so follow-ups return to the generalist.
rationale.C: Heavyweight remote delegation for in-process specialists.
rationale.D: Transferring to a sub-agent hands the conversation over, which matches a full handoff until the topic changes.

stem: In a three-agent chain, the user asks agent A, which delegates to B, which calls a tool through C. Auditors must be able to see which agent acted and on whose behalf at each hop. What supports this?

options.A: Per-agent identities whose logs record the agent and the user identity
options.B: Cloud Trace spans alone, which carry the caller's email at every hop
options.C: One shared service account with the agent name in the user-agent header
options.D: A correlation ID added by each agent to its own application logs

rationale.A: With Agent Identity, when agents act on a user's behalf logs show both the agent's and the user's identities.
rationale.B: Traces show timing and structure, not authenticated identity of each agent.
rationale.C: Headers are not authenticated identity and can be spoofed.
rationale.D: Application conventions are weaker than platform-recorded identity and are easy to omit.

stem: An architect proposes Cloud Scheduler and Pub/Sub to coordinate the steps of a user-facing agent conversation that must answer within seconds. What is the main problem?

options.A: They require a GKE cluster, which the team does not have
options.B: Pub/Sub cannot carry JSON payloads produced by agents
options.C: They are asynchronous, not request-time orchestration
options.D: Cloud Scheduler is limited to one job per project per minute

rationale.A: Both are serverless; the mismatch is architectural.
rationale.B: Pub/Sub carries arbitrary payloads; latency and ordering are the real issue.
rationale.C: Scheduling and messaging services introduce queuing and delivery latency; in-request orchestration belongs in the agent framework.
rationale.D: Not the relevant constraint.

stem: A team is tempted to build fifteen specialised agents for a workflow that today is one agent with twelve tools. Which consideration best guides the decision?

options.A: Split by model provider, so each agent uses a different vendor's model
options.B: Never split: a single agent with many tools is always simpler to operate
options.C: Always split: more agents means each prompt is shorter and therefore cheaper
options.D: Split when parts differ in ownership, deployment or scaling; otherwise keep one agent

rationale.A: Vendor diversity is not a decomposition criterion.
rationale.B: Real boundaries exist, such as different teams, runtimes or security domains.
rationale.C: Extra hops add tokens, latency and coordination failures.
rationale.D: Multi-agent decomposition pays off when boundaries are organisational or operational, not merely topical, because each hop adds latency and failure modes.

stem: A company has agents written with ADK, LangGraph and a custom framework in a container. They want one managed runtime for all of them. What is accurate about Agent Runtime?

options.A: It requires each framework to be packaged as a Gemini Enterprise agent
options.B: It supports ADK, SDK templates such as LangGraph, and any conforming container
options.C: It runs any framework but requires rewriting tools as MCP servers first
options.D: It only runs agents built with ADK in Python

rationale.A: Gemini Enterprise registration is a separate, optional step.
rationale.B: Agent Runtime provides full ADK integration, SDK templates for frameworks such as LangChain, LangGraph, AG2 and LlamaIndex, and container deployment for agents conforming to the runtime contract.
rationale.C: Not a requirement for deployment.
rationale.D: Several frameworks and container deployments are supported.

stem: A four-agent chain takes 11 seconds end to end. Traces show each agent re-reads the same 4,000-token customer profile from a tool and passes a growing transcript to the next agent. What change reduces latency most directly?

options.A: Run the four agents in parallel and merge their answers
options.B: Move all four agents into one Cloud Run revision to remove network hops
options.C: Fetch the profile once and pass a compact summary through state between agents
options.D: Increase each agent's max output tokens so fewer turns are needed

rationale.A: They are dependent steps; parallel execution would break the chain.
rationale.B: Co-location does not remove the repeated fetches or the growing context.
rationale.C: Removing repeated tool calls and shrinking inter-agent payloads cuts both tool time and token processing across every hop.
rationale.D: Longer outputs increase generation time and payload size.

stem: A new team is deciding which Agent Gateway mode to enable for two paths: developers' IDE clients calling internal agents, and those agents calling a third-party API. The architect must first state precisely which traffic each mode governs. Which description is correct?

options.A: Ingress governs clients calling agents; egress governs agents calling anything
options.B: Ingress governs agent-to-agent calls; egress governs user traffic from browsers
options.C: Ingress applies to Gemini Enterprise only; egress applies to Agent Runtime only
options.D: Ingress governs calls into Google Cloud APIs; egress governs calls to Gemini models

rationale.A: Client-to-Agent (ingress) secures clients calling agents and tools on Google Cloud; Agent-to-Anywhere (egress) secures agents calling servers, agents, tools or APIs anywhere.
rationale.B: Reverses the definitions.
rationale.C: Gemini Enterprise supports egress; Agent Runtime supports both modes.
rationale.D: Neither mode is defined by the API being called.

stem: In a sequential three-agent pipeline, the second agent's tool occasionally times out. Today the whole run fails and the user sees an error after 30 seconds. The business prefers a partial answer with a clear caveat. What design change fits?

options.A: Retry the failing tool indefinitely until it succeeds
options.B: Run the pipeline twice in parallel and use whichever run finishes
options.C: Remove the second agent so the pipeline cannot fail there
options.D: Handle the failure, degrade, and mark the gap

rationale.A: Extends the wait and can exhaust quota without ever answering.
rationale.B: Doubles cost and often fails twice for the same reason.
rationale.C: Drops the capability instead of handling the failure.
rationale.D: Explicit per-step failure handling with a degraded path lets the pipeline finish and tell the user what is missing.

stem: A remote A2A agent finishes a task and must return a generated PDF plus a short text explanation to the calling agent. Which A2A elements carry these?

options.A: Artifacts for the generated outputs, with Parts holding the file and text
options.B: A Message with role assistant carrying the PDF as base64 in its text field
options.C: The Agent Card, updated with a link to the generated file
options.D: A Task object whose ID resolves to the file in a shared bucket

rationale.A: Artifacts are tangible outputs generated during a task, and Parts are the content containers used within messages and artifacts.
rationale.B: Messages carry conversational turns; generated outputs are artifacts.
rationale.C: Agent Cards are discovery documents, not result carriers.
rationale.D: Tasks track work state; outputs are returned as artifacts.

stem: An ADK booking agent must call `check_availability` before `create_reservation`. A new prompt sometimes reverses the calls. The team wants the evaluation to fail when the order is wrong, but to tolerate an extra logging tool call. Which criterion configuration fits?

options.A: tool_trajectory_avg_score with the default EXACT match type
options.B: tool_trajectory_avg_score with the IN_ORDER match type
options.C: response_match_score with a threshold of 0.8
options.D: tool_trajectory_avg_score with the ANY_ORDER match type

rationale.A: EXACT requires a perfect match, so the additional logging call would fail the case.
rationale.B: IN_ORDER requires the reference tool calls in the specified order while allowing gaps, so an extra logging call passes but a reversal fails.
rationale.C: That compares final text to a reference, not the sequence of tool calls.
rationale.D: ANY_ORDER ignores ordering, so the reversal the team cares about would pass.

stem: A team's evalset uses response_match_score. Answers that are semantically correct but phrased differently from the reference keep scoring below the threshold, and the team wants judging based on meaning instead of word overlap. What should they use?

options.A: response_match_score with the threshold lowered to 0.3
options.B: rubric_based_tool_use_quality_v1 with a rubric about phrasing
options.C: final_response_match_v2, an LLM-judged semantic equivalence criterion
options.D: hallucinations_v1, which checks that the answer is supported by context

rationale.A: Loosening a lexical metric admits genuinely wrong answers.
rationale.B: That criterion judges tool use, not final answer equivalence.
rationale.C: final_response_match_v2 uses an LLM judge to assess semantic equivalence to the reference, unlike ROUGE-1 word overlap in response_match_score.
rationale.D: Grounding is a different property from matching a reference answer.

stem: A grounded support agent sometimes adds details that are not in the retrieved context. There is no reference answer for most cases. Which ADK criterion detects this directly?

options.A: tool_trajectory_avg_score, since ungrounded claims come from missing tool calls
options.B: response_match_score against the retrieved chunks as the reference
options.C: safety_v1, which flags harmful or non-compliant content
options.D: hallucinations_v1, which labels sentences as supported, unsupported or contradictory

rationale.A: Trajectory checks tool sequence, not whether statements are supported.
rationale.B: Comparing an answer's wording to raw chunks is not a grounding check.
rationale.C: Safety is about harmlessness, not factual grounding.
rationale.D: hallucinations_v1 evaluates response grounding against the context, segmenting sentences and labelling them, and needs no reference.

stem: A team runs `adk eval` entirely offline in a hermetic CI container with no Google Cloud project configured. Most criteria work, but one fails with an authentication error. Which criterion most likely requires the cloud?

options.A: response_match_score, which fetches the ROUGE implementation at run time
options.B: safety_v1, which delegates to the Agent Platform Eval SDK
options.C: adk conformance, which uploads baselines to the platform
options.D: tool_trajectory_avg_score, which calls the platform to compare trajectories

rationale.A: ROUGE-1 overlap is computed locally.
rationale.B: safety_v1 delegates to the Agent Platform Eval SDK and requires Google Cloud setup, unlike purely local criteria.
rationale.C: Conformance compares against a local golden baseline.
rationale.D: Trajectory matching is computed locally without an LLM judge.

stem: A legal-drafting agent must be judged on criteria specific to the firm: correct clause ordering, no advice outside jurisdiction, and a formal tone. There is no single reference answer. Which ADK criterion family fits?

options.A: tool_trajectory_avg_score with a rubric attached to each case
options.B: response_match_score with several accepted reference answers
options.C: rubric_based_final_response_quality_v1 with custom rubrics
options.D: hallucinations_v1 with the firm's style guide as context

rationale.A: Trajectory criteria judge tool calls, not drafting quality.
rationale.B: Lexical matching cannot express jurisdiction or tone requirements.
rationale.C: Rubric-based criteria evaluate quality against custom rubrics with an LLM judge and need no reference response.
rationale.D: Grounding checks support for claims, not stylistic rubrics.

stem: A concierge agent behaves well on single-turn cases but loses track of constraints across a ten-turn booking conversation. The team wants to measure whether the whole conversation achieves the user's goal. Which criterion fits?

options.A: multi_turn_task_success_v1, measuring goal achievement
options.B: final_response_match_v2 applied to the last turn only
options.C: response_match_score averaged over all ten turns
options.D: per_turn_user_simulator_quality_v1 on the agent's replies

rationale.A: multi_turn_task_success_v1 measures whether the conversation achieved the goal, using the Agent Platform Eval SDK.
rationale.B: Judging only the final message misses failures earlier in the conversation.
rationale.C: Word overlap per turn does not indicate whether the goal was met.
rationale.D: That criterion validates the user simulator's fidelity, not the agent's success.

stem: Before a risky refactor of an agent's tools, a team wants a recorded baseline of current behaviour so any deviation after the refactor is flagged automatically. Which ADK capability is designed for this?

options.A: adk eval with safety_v1 across the existing evalset
options.B: adk conformance, which compares behaviour against a golden baseline
options.C: adk deploy agent_engine with traffic splitting between versions
options.D: adk web's Eval tab, replaying cases by hand after the refactor

rationale.A: Safety scoring does not capture behavioural deviation from a baseline.
rationale.B: adk conformance runs regression checks against a recorded golden baseline.
rationale.C: Deployment strategy is not a behavioural baseline comparison.
rationale.D: Manual replay is not an automated regression gate.

stem: A new team member has been asked to add regression cases for a booking agent and opens the project's existing ADK evalset file for the first time. Before writing cases they need to know what each case in that file records. What is the correct answer?

options.A: Model weights and a random seed so runs are reproducible
options.B: Only the user prompt and the expected final text, with tools inferred
options.C: Production traces exported from Cloud Trace in OpenTelemetry format
options.D: User turns with the expected tool trajectory and a reference response

rationale.A: Evalsets contain cases, not model artefacts.
rationale.B: Expected tool calls are part of the case, enabling trajectory scoring.
rationale.C: Traces are observability data, not evalset cases.
rationale.D: ADK eval cases record the user input, the expected tool trajectory and a reference response for scoring.

stem: A team using the Gen AI evaluation service wants a metric that returns 1 only when the agent's tool calls are exactly the reference calls, in the same order, with nothing extra. Which metric is that?

options.A: trajectory_any_order_match
options.B: trajectory_precision
options.C: trajectory_exact_match
options.D: trajectory_in_order_match

rationale.A: That ignores order and tolerates extras.
rationale.B: Precision measures how many predicted calls were relevant, returning a float rather than a strict match.
rationale.C: trajectory_exact_match returns 1 only when the predicted trajectory is identical to the reference, with the same calls in the same order.
rationale.D: That tolerates extra tool calls as long as reference calls appear in order.

stem: An agent completes tasks correctly but calls several unnecessary tools on the way, raising cost. The team wants a number that reflects how many of its calls were actually relevant. Which metric fits?

options.A: trajectory_precision, which measures how many predicted calls were relevant
options.B: trajectory_in_order_match, which returns 0 when extra calls appear
options.C: trajectory_single_tool_use, which checks that only one tool was used
options.D: trajectory_exact_match, which penalises every deviation equally

rationale.A: trajectory_precision measures how many of the predicted trajectory's tool calls are relevant according to the reference, returning a value between 0 and 1.
rationale.B: It tolerates extra calls and returns a binary result.
rationale.C: It checks whether a specified tool was used, not overall relevance.
rationale.D: Binary and blunt; it cannot quantify how many calls were unnecessary.

stem: A compliance rule says a particular agent must always consult the `policy_lookup` tool at least once per conversation, regardless of order or how many other tools it uses. Which metric expresses this?

options.A: trajectory_any_order_match against a reference containing policy_lookup
options.B: trajectory_recall over the full reference trajectory
options.C: trajectory_single_tool_use with policy_lookup named in the metric spec
options.D: trajectory_exact_match with a one-call reference

rationale.A: That requires all reference calls, not just the one tool of interest.
rationale.B: Recall measures coverage of all reference calls.
rationale.C: trajectory_single_tool_use checks whether a specified tool appears in the predicted trajectory, ignoring order and count.
rationale.D: That would fail whenever the agent uses any other tool.

stem: After an evaluation run on the Gen AI evaluation service, a team sees two result columns they did not configure: response time and an error indicator. What are they?

options.A: Metrics inherited from the previous run in the same project
options.B: Default agent performance metrics: latency and whether the invocation failed
options.C: Leftover columns from the dataset's schema that should be removed
options.D: Placeholders that must be populated by a custom autorater

rationale.A: Results are per run; these two are defaults.
rationale.B: Two agent performance metrics are added by default: the time taken to return a response and a boolean indicating whether the invocation errored.
rationale.C: They are added by the service, not by the dataset.
rationale.D: They are computed automatically.

stem: A team already has production traces with the user's prompt, the tool calls the agent made, and its answer, plus curated expected tool calls. They want to score these without re-running the agent. What do they need?

options.A: A bring-your-own dataset with prompt, reference and predicted trajectories and response
options.B: To convert the traces into an ADK evalset, the only supported input format
options.C: To re-run the agent through the service, because only live runs can be scored
options.D: To label each trace manually with a pass or fail before uploading

rationale.A: The evaluation service accepts datasets containing prompt, reference_trajectory, predicted_trajectory and response, so recorded runs can be scored directly.
rationale.B: The service accepts its own dataset format.
rationale.C: Bring-your-own-dataset evaluation is supported.
rationale.D: Manual labels are not required for the computed metrics.

stem: A team is assembling its first golden dataset for a claims agent. They plan to sample 200 typical conversations from production. A reviewer warns this will hide the failures they most care about. What should they add?

options.A: Synthetic paraphrases of the same 200 conversations
options.B: Only the conversations that received low customer satisfaction scores
options.C: Another 2,000 typical conversations so rare cases appear by chance
options.D: Edge cases: rare claim types, ambiguous inputs, hostile users and tool failures

rationale.A: Paraphrases test wording robustness, not unusual situations.
rationale.B: Useful, but a biased set that omits silent failures and happy paths.
rationale.C: Scaling typical traffic buries rare cases in noise and cost.
rationale.D: The guide calls for test sets containing golden data, prompts and edge cases, because typical traffic does not exercise failure modes.

stem: An agent passes its evalset in CI, yet quality complaints rise two months after launch as user phrasing and the product catalogue change. Which practice addresses this specific gap?

options.A: Continuous evaluation on sampled production traffic against the golden set
options.B: Adding more unit tests for the agent's tool functions
options.C: Raising the CI pass threshold from 80% to 95%
options.D: Running the same CI evalset more frequently, for example hourly

rationale.A: Continuous evaluation pipelines detect drift after release, which a fixed pre-merge suite cannot see.
rationale.B: Unit tests verify code, not agent behaviour against changing inputs.
rationale.C: A stricter gate on stale cases does not detect drift.
rationale.D: The same fixed cases cannot reveal changes in real traffic.

stem: A team wants every pull request that changes prompts or tools to be blocked when the agent's tool trajectory regresses. What should they implement?

options.A: Canary deployment with 5% traffic and manual monitoring
options.B: An evalset run in the CI pipeline that fails the build below threshold
options.C: A linter that checks prompt files for forbidden words
options.D: A weekly manual review of agent transcripts by the team lead

rationale.A: Catches problems after merge and in production.
rationale.B: Continuous evaluation pipelines assess tool execution against established success criteria as part of the merge gate.
rationale.C: Static checks cannot detect behavioural regressions.
rationale.D: Too slow and not a merge gate.

stem: A RAG agent's answers are judged wrong by evaluators, but nobody can tell whether retrieval failed or the model misused good context. What evaluation design resolves this ambiguity?

options.A: Evaluate only the final answer, since that is what users see
options.B: Replace the LLM judge with human judges for all cases
options.C: Increase the number of evaluators reviewing each answer
options.D: Score retrieval and response quality separately for each case

rationale.A: That is exactly the setup that hides which stage failed.
rationale.B: Changes who judges, not what is measured.
rationale.C: More reviewers on the same signal still cannot separate the causes.
rationale.D: The guide asks for evaluating agent response and retrieval quality against a golden dataset, which separates the two failure modes.

stem: A team reports that hallucinations_v1 and response_match_score 'use the same 0.8 setting', and asks what that number means in each case. Which explanation is correct?

options.A: It is the sampling rate of cases sent to the LLM judge
options.B: It is a global confidence level applied to every criterion in the evalset
options.C: Each criterion has its own threshold above which a case passes
options.D: It is the fraction of evalset cases that must pass overall

rationale.A: Thresholds are not sampling rates.
rationale.B: Thresholds are per criterion, not one global setting.
rationale.C: Criteria define their own default thresholds, for example 0.8 for response_match_score and for hallucinations_v1, applied to that criterion's score.
rationale.D: The threshold applies per case score, not to the suite pass rate.

stem: An LLM-judged criterion gives slightly different verdicts on re-runs of the same case, making CI flaky. Which property of final_response_match_v2 helps, and what else should the team do?

options.A: It falls back to response_match_score when the judge is uncertain
options.B: It runs the judge at temperature zero, which removes all variance
options.C: It caches judgements per case, so the first verdict is reused forever
options.D: It majority-votes several judge samples; keep cases decisive

rationale.A: No such fallback is described.
rationale.B: Determinism is not guaranteed and is not how the criterion is described.
rationale.C: Caching verdicts would hide genuine regressions.
rationale.D: final_response_match_v2 uses multiple sampling with a majority vote, configurable by judge model and sample count, and unambiguous cases reduce residual variance.

stem: During evaluation a team finds the agent fails on a family of rare requests. They want to supply curated examples of correct handling that the agent can retrieve at run time, rather than fine-tuning. Which platform feature supports this?

options.A: Example Store on Agent Runtime, retrieving relevant examples at run time
options.B: The evalset file, which is loaded into the prompt at run time
options.C: Memory Bank, storing the examples as user memories
options.D: Model Garden, which hosts tuned variants of the base model

rationale.A: Example Store stores and retrieves examples used to improve agent behaviour.
rationale.B: Evalsets are test data, not run-time context.
rationale.C: Memory Bank holds user-scoped facts from conversations, not curated exemplars.
rationale.D: That is model hosting, not example retrieval.

stem: A retailer's definition of a 'good' answer includes brand-voice rules no standard metric captures. They want scalable automated scoring aligned with their reviewers' judgements. What should they do?

options.A: Switch to a larger model and assume tone improves
options.B: Have reviewers score every production answer by hand each week
options.C: Customise the autorater with adaptive rubrics reflecting the brand rules
options.D: Use trajectory metrics as a proxy, since good tool use implies good tone

rationale.A: No measurement, and no alignment with the firm's rules.
rationale.B: Does not scale, which was the requirement.
rationale.C: The evaluation service supports autorater customisation and adaptive rubrics so teams can tailor criteria to their requirements.
rationale.D: Tool use says nothing about brand voice.

stem: An evaluation run fails 180 of 500 cases. Before fixing anything, the team wants to know whether these failures fall into a few recurring patterns. Which Agents CLI command helps?

options.A: agents-cli eval compare, run against the same result file twice
options.B: agents-cli eval analyze, which clusters failures from a run result
options.C: agents-cli eval grade with a stricter metric set
options.D: agents-cli eval metric list to see which metrics failed

rationale.A: compare diffs two result files; it does not cluster failures.
rationale.B: eval analyze (experimental) analyses failure clusters from an evaluation run result.
rationale.C: Re-grading changes scores, not failure analysis.
rationale.D: It lists available metrics, not failures.

stem: A payments agent must never call `issue_refund` without first calling `verify_identity`. Which evaluation approach best enforces this as a release criterion?

options.A: Manual review of a sample of refunds each month
options.B: Trajectory evaluation cases asserting verify_identity precedes issue_refund
options.C: A rubric asking a judge whether the answer sounds compliant
options.D: An alert on refunds issued without a preceding verification log entry

rationale.A: Sampling after the fact is not a release gate.
rationale.B: Continuous evaluation of tool execution against success criteria catches ordering violations before release.
rationale.C: Judging tone does not verify the call sequence.
rationale.D: Production detection, not pre-release prevention.

stem: Over a year, an agent's evalset has grown to 4,000 cases, many added after incidents. Runs now take hours and engineers skip them. Which change best preserves signal while restoring speed?

options.A: Delete the oldest 3,000 cases, keeping only recent incidents
options.B: Run the full suite only before quarterly releases
options.C: Replace the suite with a single end-to-end smoke test
options.D: Tier it: a fast gate per PR, the full suite nightly

rationale.A: Throws away regression coverage for old failures.
rationale.B: Feedback arrives far too late to be actionable.
rationale.C: Loses almost all behavioural coverage.
rationale.D: Splitting into a fast merge gate and a comprehensive scheduled run keeps feedback quick without discarding coverage.

stem: A team wants to judge whether the agent chose sensible tools with sensible parameters, even when no single reference trajectory is correct because several tool sequences are acceptable. Which criterion is appropriate?

options.A: tool_trajectory_avg_score with ANY_ORDER
options.B: trajectory_recall over a union of all acceptable trajectories
options.C: rubric_based_tool_use_quality_v1 with custom rubrics
options.D: hallucinations_v1 on the tool outputs

rationale.A: Still requires a specific set of reference calls.
rationale.B: Merging alternatives into one reference rewards calling everything.
rationale.C: That criterion uses custom rubrics and an LLM judge to assess tool selection, parameters and sequencing without requiring a reference.
rationale.D: Grounding of text, not quality of tool choice.

stem: A team has automated its agent evaluation with an LLM judge and now wants to use those scores as a release gate. Leadership asks what evidence shows the judge's verdicts match what the company considers a good answer. Which practice most directly establishes that?

options.A: Periodically compare judge verdicts with human labels on a sample
options.B: Average three different judge models to remove bias
options.C: Use the largest available model as the judge and accept its verdicts
options.D: Have the agent being evaluated review the judge's explanations

rationale.A: Calibrating the autorater against human judgement is what justifies relying on it at scale.
rationale.B: Ensembling may reduce variance but still lacks a human reference point.
rationale.C: Model size alone does not demonstrate agreement with human standards.
rationale.D: Self-review by the system under test is not evidence.

stem: LLM-judged criteria on 4,000 cases per run have become the team's largest AI spend. They must cut cost without losing the ability to catch regressions. Which approach is best?

options.A: Use cheap deterministic criteria broadly and LLM judges on a focused subset
options.B: Reduce the judge's sample count to one and keep all 4,000 cases judged
options.C: Judge every case with a smaller model without checking agreement
options.D: Run evaluation only on release branches

rationale.A: Deterministic criteria such as trajectory matching are inexpensive and catch many regressions; reserve judge-based scoring for cases that need semantic judgement.
rationale.B: Cuts cost but increases verdict variance and flakiness.
rationale.C: May silently change what counts as a pass.
rationale.D: Delays detection until integration, when fixes are costlier.

stem: A company runs agents on Agent Runtime, a LangChain agent in Cloud Run, and a bespoke Python agent. Platform engineering wants one evaluation service for all three. Is that possible with the Gen AI evaluation service?

options.A: Only for ADK agents, since trajectories come from ADK events
options.B: Only if all agents are re-registered in Gemini Enterprise first
options.C: Yes: Agent Runtime, LangChain and custom agents
options.D: Only for agents deployed on Agent Runtime

rationale.A: Trajectories can be supplied in the dataset.
rationale.B: Registration there is unrelated to evaluation support.
rationale.C: The documentation lists Agent Runtime, LangChain and custom agents as compatible.
rationale.D: Custom and LangChain agents are supported too.

stem: A team generates multi-turn evaluation conversations with a simulated user. Before trusting the results, they want to check that the simulated user followed the intended conversation plan rather than drifting into unrelated requests. Which criterion applies?

options.A: multi_turn_task_success_v1 on the conversation outcome
options.B: hallucinations_v1 applied to the simulated user's messages
options.C: multi_turn_trajectory_quality_v1 on the agent's tool calls
options.D: per_turn_user_simulator_quality_v1

rationale.A: Outcome success does not confirm the simulator behaved as planned.
rationale.B: Grounding of agent responses is a different property.
rationale.C: That assesses the agent's interaction quality, not the simulator.
rationale.D: per_turn_user_simulator_quality_v1 validates that the user simulator stayed faithful to the conversation plan.

stem: After a prompt change, 30 evaluation cases fail. The team has limited time before a release. What is the most effective triage order?

options.A: Lower thresholds until the 30 cases pass, then release
options.B: Group failures by cause and fix critical flows first
options.C: Disable the 30 failing cases and revisit them after release
options.D: Fix cases in the order they appear in the evalset file

rationale.A: Hides the regression rather than fixing it.
rationale.B: Clustering by cause and business impact fixes the most important failures first instead of scanning cases one by one.
rationale.C: Removes the signal that something regressed.
rationale.D: File order has no relationship to risk.

stem: A product manager without a Python environment wants to try evaluation cases against the agent during a working session with the team. Which ADK affordance suits them?

options.A: adk eval on the command line with a JSON config file
options.B: Agent Designer's preview pane in Gemini Enterprise
options.C: The Agent Runtime console's deployment page
options.D: The Eval tab in the adk web development UI

rationale.A: Requires the environment the manager does not have.
rationale.B: A different product for no-code agents.
rationale.C: That manages deployments, not evaluation cases.
rationale.D: adk web provides a development UI including an Eval tab for running evaluation cases interactively.

stem: An architect must pick the primary metric for a customer-facing FAQ agent whose main risk is confidently inventing policy details. Which choice best matches the risk?

options.A: Average response latency across the evalset
options.B: A grounding metric that flags unsupported statements
options.C: Token cost per answer as a proxy for verbosity
options.D: Tool trajectory exact match against a reference

rationale.A: Speed does not address invented content.
rationale.B: The named risk is fabrication, which grounding metrics measure directly.
rationale.C: Cost tells nothing about factual support.
rationale.D: An FAQ agent's risk is content, not tool ordering.

stem: After running evaluations, a team needs to show stakeholders where the agent is weak and how it changed since last month. What does the evaluation service provide?

options.A: A guaranteed production quality score for the next 30 days
options.B: Automatic pull requests that fix the failing behaviours
options.C: Visualisation of results to interpret strengths and failure modes
options.D: Direct comparison against competitors' agents

rationale.A: Evaluation reports measured results, not forecasts.
rationale.B: Not a capability of the evaluation service.
rationale.C: The service provides visualisation capabilities to view and interpret evaluation results.
rationale.D: No such benchmark is provided.

stem: A team wants continuous evaluation over production traffic but cannot afford to judge every conversation, and must still detect regressions in rare high-value flows. What sampling design fits?

options.A: Stratified sampling, weighted toward rare critical flows
options.B: Judging the first 100 conversations each morning
options.C: Uniform random sampling of 1% of all conversations
options.D: Judging only conversations that users rated badly

rationale.A: Stratification keeps evaluation affordable while ensuring rare but important flows are represented.
rationale.B: Time-of-day bias and no coverage guarantee for critical flows.
rationale.C: Rare critical flows may never be sampled.
rationale.D: Misses silent failures users never report.

stem: Engineering says evaluation cases belong to product, product says they belong to engineering, and the suite is drifting from what the business cares about. Which practice resolves this most directly?

options.A: Product writes cases directly in the evaluation file format
options.B: Engineering writes all cases from the product requirements document
options.C: Domain experts curate answers; engineers own the harness
options.D: Generate all cases synthetically from production logs

rationale.A: A tooling barrier that usually stalls contributions.
rationale.B: Requirements documents go stale and engineers lack domain nuance.
rationale.C: Splitting responsibility by expertise keeps cases business-relevant and the pipeline maintained.
rationale.D: Useful input, but nobody validates what correct looks like.

stem: A five-person startup is launching its first production agent. It needs managed conversation state, long-term memory and built-in tracing, has no platform engineers, and wants to spend its time on agent logic. Which runtime should it choose?

options.A: Cloud Run, adding Firestore for sessions and a custom memory service
options.B: Compute Engine instances behind a load balancer, scaled manually
options.C: GKE with a dedicated node pool and a service mesh for the agent
options.D: Agent Runtime, with managed sessions, memory and observability

rationale.A: Workable, but the team must build and operate state and memory themselves.
rationale.B: The heaviest operational burden of all the options.
rationale.C: Maximum control and maximum operations for a team with no platform engineers.
rationale.D: Agent Runtime is the fully managed option and includes Sessions, Memory Bank, code execution and observability without infrastructure work.

stem: A company already builds every service as a container with an existing CI pipeline, security scanning and a private base image. Its new agent must fit that pipeline, scale to zero overnight and expose an HTTPS endpoint. State is handled by an existing managed session store. Which runtime fits best?

options.A: Cloud Run, which runs the team's own container and scales to zero
options.B: Agent Runtime, migrating the pipeline to its SDK-based deployment
options.C: Agent Runtime code execution sandboxes as the serving layer
options.D: GKE Autopilot with a Deployment and an Ingress for the agent

rationale.A: Cloud Run suits existing container pipelines, HTTP serving and scale-to-zero for bursty traffic.
rationale.B: Possible, but it sets aside the container pipeline the company standardised on.
rationale.C: Sandboxes execute generated code; they are not a serving runtime.
rationale.D: More platform surface than needed when a serverless container runtime suffices.

stem: An agent must run alongside a sidecar that holds a hardware security module session, use GPU nodes for a self-hosted embedding model, and enforce node-level network policy. The company already runs GKE. Which runtime is appropriate?

options.A: Agent Runtime, with the HSM session held in Memory Bank
options.B: GKE, which supports sidecars, GPU node pools and network policy
options.C: Cloud Run with a multi-container revision and GPU allocation
options.D: Cloud Functions triggered per request, with the model loaded per invocation

rationale.A: Memory Bank stores memories, not hardware security module sessions, and Runtime does not expose node controls.
rationale.B: GKE is the choice when the workload needs sidecars, node-level control or GPUs that managed runtimes do not expose.
rationale.C: Cloud Run does not give node-level network policy or the cluster controls described.
rationale.D: Cold-loading an embedding model per request is unworkable.

stem: A team's agent uses an unusual Python framework and a set of system packages. They want it on Agent Runtime without rewriting it to an SDK template. What deployment option exists?

options.A: A container image from Artifact Registry meeting the contract
options.B: Rewrite the agent with ADK, the only supported entry point
options.C: Package the agent as a Skill Registry skill and let the runtime load it
options.D: Deploy to Cloud Run and register the URL as an Agent Runtime instance

rationale.A: Agent Runtime accepts a container image from Artifact Registry, or a Dockerfile with source, for agents outside the supported SDK templates.
rationale.B: Container deployment is supported alongside ADK and SDK templates.
rationale.C: Skills are agent capabilities, not deployable runtime units.
rationale.D: That is a different runtime, not a way of deploying to Agent Runtime.

stem: A regulated customer requires that an agent on Agent Runtime reach an internal API over private networking, that data at rest use the customer's own keys, and that the deployment sit inside a service perimeter. Which statement is correct?

options.A: Private networking requires deploying the agent inside the customer's own VPC on GKE
options.B: Agent Runtime supports Private Service Connect interfaces, CMEK and VPC Service Controls
options.C: Only VPC Service Controls is supported; private networking requires Cloud Run
options.D: Customer-managed keys are unavailable, so the customer must accept Google-managed keys

rationale.A: PSC interfaces provide private connectivity without moving to GKE.
rationale.B: Agent Runtime documents PSC interface networking, CMEK configuration and VPC-SC compliance.
rationale.C: PSC interfaces are supported on Agent Runtime.
rationale.D: CMEK configuration is available.

stem: A developer finished an ADK agent locally and asks which deploy targets the ADK CLI offers out of the box. What should you tell them?

options.A: Only Cloud Run, with Agent Runtime reserved for no-code agents
options.B: App Engine standard and Cloud Functions
options.C: Docker, Cloud Run and Agent Runtime via the ADK CLI
options.D: Only Agent Runtime, since ADK agents cannot run in containers

rationale.A: Agent Runtime is a first-class ADK deployment target.
rationale.B: Not the documented ADK deploy targets.
rationale.C: adk deploy supports docker, cloud_run and agent_engine targets, with options such as --with_ui.
rationale.D: ADK supports container and Cloud Run deployment too.

stem: An internal agent is used heavily between 09:00 and 11:00 and almost never at night. The team pays for provisioned capacity around the clock on their current platform, and cold starts during the morning peak are hurting first-response latency. What is the best approach?

options.A: Schedule a nightly batch job to pre-compute the morning's answers
options.B: Scale purely on demand with no warm instances and accept cold starts
options.C: Keep capacity provisioned for peak at all times to guarantee latency
options.D: Serverless scaling with a small warm floor sized for the morning ramp

rationale.A: Agent conversations cannot be pre-computed.
rationale.B: Leaves the morning latency problem unsolved.
rationale.C: Pays for idle capacity for most of the day, which is the current complaint.
rationale.D: Scale-to-zero removes idle cost while a minimal warm pool absorbs cold starts during the known peak.

stem: A team wants one command that deploys their agent to the target configured for the project, and a way to check on a long-running deployment later. What does Agents CLI provide?

options.A: agents-cli deploy with options such as --no-wait and --status
options.B: agents-cli publish, which deploys and then reports status
options.C: agents-cli infra single-project, which deploys the agent with Terraform
options.D: agents-cli run --url, which deploys the agent behind a URL

rationale.A: agents-cli deploy deploys to the configured target and supports --list, --no-wait and --status for ongoing deployments.
rationale.B: publish registers a deployed agent with Gemini Enterprise.
rationale.C: It provisions infrastructure and IAM, not the agent deployment itself.
rationale.D: run sends a single prompt to a local or deployed agent.

stem: An agent on Cloud Run has outgrown its hand-rolled session and memory code, which now causes most incidents. The team wants to keep its container build but stop maintaining state code. What is the pragmatic path?

options.A: Rewrite the agent in ADK and deploy to Agent Runtime immediately
options.B: Move state into the container's local disk to simplify the architecture
options.C: Add a Memorystore cache in front of the existing session code
options.D: Keep the container and adopt managed Sessions and Memory Bank for state

rationale.A: A full rewrite is a large step when only state management is the problem.
rationale.B: Local disk is lost on restart and breaks with multiple instances.
rationale.C: A cache does not remove the custom state code or its bugs.
rationale.D: Managed session and memory services can be used from an agent running elsewhere, removing the custom code without a rewrite.

stem: A voice assistant needs tokens streamed back as they are produced, in both directions, from an agent hosted on Agent Runtime. Is this supported?

options.A: No: responses are returned only when the full answer is ready
options.B: Yes: Agent Runtime supports bidirectional streaming
options.C: Only when the agent is deployed as a container rather than with the SDK
options.D: Only through Gemini Enterprise's chat interface

rationale.A: Streaming is supported.
rationale.B: Agent Runtime documents bidirectional streaming support.
rationale.C: Streaming is not restricted to container deployments.
rationale.D: Streaming is a runtime capability, not limited to that interface.

stem: A team deployed an ADK agent to Agent Runtime and sees logs but no traces in the console's Traces tab. They expected step-by-step spans. What is the most likely cause?

options.A: Traces appear only after 10,000 requests have been recorded
options.B: ADK agents cannot be traced; only custom frameworks emit spans
options.C: Telemetry was not enabled at deploy time for the AdkApp
options.D: Cloud Trace must be replaced by a self-hosted Jaeger backend for agents

rationale.A: There is no such threshold.
rationale.B: ADK applications can be instrumented with OpenTelemetry.
rationale.C: Tracing requires enabling OpenTelemetry for the deployed app, for example the telemetry environment variable set when deploying to Agent Runtime.
rationale.D: Agent traces are exported to Google Cloud Observability.

stem: During an incident, an on-call engineer needs to see the exact sequence of model and tool calls for one slow user session, including inputs and outputs per step. Which view should they open?

options.A: The Logs tab, filtered to the session's severity levels
options.B: The Usage dashboard, filtered to the session's tokens
options.C: The evaluation results for the most recent run
options.D: The agent's Traces tab, showing spans for that session as a graph

rationale.A: Logs give a raw stream, not the per-step span structure.
rationale.B: Usage shows infrastructure-level metrics, not per-step execution.
rationale.C: Evaluation reports on test cases, not a live session.
rationale.D: The Traces tab inspects step-by-step execution of specific sessions, including directed acyclic graphs of spans and inputs and outputs.

stem: A finance stakeholder asks which dashboard shows an agent's container CPU and memory allocation alongside token usage. Where should you point them?

options.A: The Usage dashboards, which show runtime metrics and token usage
options.B: Cloud Billing reports broken down by agent name
options.C: The Traces tab, which aggregates token counts per span
options.D: The Logs tab with a query on the token field

rationale.A: Usage dashboards provide infrastructure-level metrics for the agent's runtime environment, including container CPU, memory and token usage.
rationale.B: Billing shows spend, not container allocation or token metrics per agent.
rationale.C: Traces show execution structure for individual sessions.
rationale.D: Log queries are not the dashboard for these metrics.

stem: Traces for a support agent show the same `lookup_order` call with identical arguments seven times in one session before the agent gives up. What is the failure, and which fix addresses it most directly?

options.A: Session state corruption: clear the session store and retry
options.B: Model drift: retrain or switch to a newer model version
options.C: A reasoning loop: cap iterations and handle the empty result explicitly
options.D: Tool latency: increase the tool's timeout so the agent waits longer

rationale.A: Nothing indicates corrupted state, and clearing it loses history.
rationale.B: Drift is a gradual quality change, not repeated identical calls in one session.
rationale.C: Repeated identical tool calls indicate a loop; bounding iterations and giving the model a defined path for empty results breaks it.
rationale.D: The calls complete; the agent simply repeats them.

stem: An agent's p95 response time is 9 seconds. Traces show the model spans total about 1.2 seconds, while a single `search_knowledge_base` span takes 6 to 7 seconds on most requests. What should the team do first?

options.A: Shorten the system prompt to reduce token processing time
options.B: Optimise the knowledge-base tool, since it dominates the latency budget
options.C: Increase the agent's concurrency so more requests run in parallel
options.D: Switch to a smaller, faster model to cut total latency

rationale.A: Prompt length is not what makes this request slow.
rationale.B: Trace spans attribute time per call; the bottleneck is the tool, not the model.
rationale.C: Concurrency changes throughput, not the latency of one request.
rationale.D: Model time is a small share; the gain would be marginal.

stem: Over six weeks, an agent's answer quality slowly declines although no code, prompt or model version changed. Traffic mix has shifted toward a newly launched product line. What is happening, and what detects it?

options.A: Model deprecation: pin the model to an older version
options.B: Input drift, detected by continuous production evaluation
options.C: Prompt injection: enable Model Armor on the agent
options.D: A memory leak in the runtime: restart the instances weekly

rationale.A: The model version did not change in this scenario.
rationale.B: Behaviour degrades as real inputs move away from what the agent was built and tested for; sampled production evaluation is what surfaces this.
rationale.C: Nothing indicates malicious input; the mix of legitimate topics changed.
rationale.D: Infrastructure restarts do not change answer quality.

stem: A grounded agent occasionally states product limits that do not appear in any retrieved document. A colleague proposes enabling Model Armor to stop it. What is the correct assessment?

options.A: Model Armor screens injection and safety, not grounding
options.B: Correct, provided inspect-and-block mode is enabled for responses
options.C: Correct: enabling the Sensitive Data Protection filter removes invented details
options.D: Correct: Model Armor's responsible-AI filters block unsupported claims

rationale.A: Model Armor's filters target prompt injection, responsible-AI categories, sensitive data and malicious URLs, not whether a claim is supported by context.
rationale.B: Enforcement mode does not give Model Armor a grounding capability.
rationale.C: SDP detects sensitive data, not fabrication.
rationale.D: Those filters cover harmful content categories, not factuality.

stem: An agent that worked in staging fails in production with 'Egress request is not authorized' when calling an external API through Agent Gateway. Which two checks are most relevant? (Choose two.)

options.A: Whether an authorization policy allows this agent to reach that destination
options.B: Whether the agent identity has the roles required for gateway egress
options.C: Whether the model version used in production differs from staging
options.D: Whether the agent's session store has capacity for new sessions
options.E: Whether the destination's DNS record resolves inside the VPC

rationale.A: Agent Gateway requires an authorization policy permitting the agent-destination pair.
rationale.B: Egress authorization failures are commonly missing IAM permissions for the agent identity.
rationale.C: Model choice does not affect gateway authorization.
rationale.D: Session capacity is unrelated to egress authorization.
rationale.E: The error is an authorization decision, not a name-resolution failure.

stem: An engineer must find all errors emitted by one deployed agent across the last hour, with severity and timestamps, to reconstruct a failure. Which tool fits best?

options.A: Cloud Monitoring uptime checks on the agent endpoint
options.B: The Traces tab, scanning every session from the last hour
options.C: The Logs view, filtered by resource and severity
options.D: The evaluation dashboard for the agent's latest run

rationale.A: Uptime checks show availability, not error detail.
rationale.B: Traces are per session; scanning them all is impractical for a sweep.
rationale.C: Logs display a filterable stream of raw agent logs including severity, timestamps and execution summaries for troubleshooting.
rationale.D: Evaluation covers test cases, not production errors.

stem: A payments agent intermittently returns a generic apology. Traces show a tool span with status error and no retry, and the model was given the raw stack trace as the tool result. What should change?

options.A: Instruct the model to apologise more specifically when a tool fails
options.B: Suppress tool errors so the model never sees them
options.C: Increase the model's temperature so it explores alternative phrasings
options.D: Return a structured error the model can act on, and retry transient failures

rationale.A: Improves wording without improving behaviour.
rationale.B: Hiding failures produces confident wrong answers.
rationale.C: Sampling settings do not handle tool failures.
rationale.D: Tools should surface actionable, structured errors with retries for transient faults so the agent can recover or explain precisely.
