stem: An agent's monthly model spend doubled after a release. Traces show the system prompt grew to 12,000 tokens because the team pasted the full policy handbook into it, and most questions need only one section. What is the most effective change?

options.A: Switch to a cheaper model and keep the 12,000-token prompt
options.B: Retrieve the relevant policy section per request
options.C: Trim the handbook by deleting older policies
options.D: Cache the prompt locally in the agent container

rationale.A: Still pays for the same tokens and lowers quality.
rationale.B: Moving rarely needed content out of the prompt into retrieval cuts input tokens on every request.
rationale.C: Loses coverage and only slightly reduces the prompt.
rationale.D: Local caching does not reduce tokens sent to the model.

stem: After a regional incident, an agent returned errors for 40 minutes. The postmortem asks how to reduce impact next time without doubling steady-state cost. Which measure fits best?

options.A: Degrade gracefully with caching and reduced capability
options.B: Retry failed requests indefinitely until the region recovers
options.C: Send users to a status page and disable the agent during incidents
options.D: Run a hot standby of the full stack in a second region at all times

rationale.A: A defined degraded mode keeps partial service without running full duplicate capacity at all times.
rationale.B: Amplifies load and leaves users waiting.
rationale.C: No service at all, when partial service was achievable.
rationale.D: Meets availability but doubles steady-state cost, which was excluded.

stem: A team runs a non-ADK custom agent on Agent Runtime and wants the same traces and dashboards as their ADK agents. What must they do?

options.A: Rewrite the agent with ADK, the only framework that can be traced
options.B: Export logs to BigQuery and rebuild the dashboards there
options.C: Nothing: Agent Runtime instruments any deployed agent automatically
options.D: Instrument the app to emit OpenTelemetry telemetry

rationale.A: Non-ADK agents can be instrumented too.
rationale.B: Duplicates tooling instead of using the platform's observability.
rationale.C: Built-in components emit telemetry, but custom applications must be instrumented.
rationale.D: Agents must be configured to send telemetry in the OpenTelemetry format to populate observability dashboards, topologies and traces; docs cover instrumenting non-ADK agents.

stem: A security engineer asks what happens to user requests if Model Armor cannot be reached while screening is configured. What should you tell them, and what should follow?

options.A: Requests are queued and screened retroactively when it recovers
options.B: All requests are blocked until Model Armor recovers, so plan for downtime
options.C: The request proceeds unscreened, so add alerting on screening failures
options.D: The agent automatically switches to a local filter model

rationale.A: There is no retroactive screening queue.
rationale.B: Screening failures do not block traffic by default.
rationale.C: If Model Armor is unreachable the request continues without screening, so teams need monitoring to detect the gap.
rationale.D: No such fallback exists.

stem: An agent computes shipping dates and is occasionally off by one day for orders placed late at night. Traces show the model called the date tool correctly with the values it was given. Where is the defect most likely?

options.A: In the retrieval corpus, which lacks a shipping-policy document
options.B: In the tool's own timezone handling, not in the model's reasoning
options.C: In the model's arithmetic, which should be replaced with a larger model
options.D: In the session state, which loses the order timestamp overnight

rationale.A: This is a computation defect, not a knowledge gap.
rationale.B: When tool inputs are correct and outputs are wrong, the defect is in the tool implementation, which ordinary unit tests can catch.
rationale.C: The model delegated the computation to the tool.
rationale.D: The tool received the values, so state carried them.

stem: A newly launched agent shows three symptoms: occasional 10-second responses, one tool failing 5% of the time, and rising cost. The team has one week. Which approach gives the most reliable improvement?

options.A: Escalate to the model provider before investigating internally
options.B: Start with the cheapest fix regardless of impact
options.C: Fix all three at once with a single large refactor
options.D: Quantify each symptom from traces and fix in order of user impact

rationale.A: The symptoms point at the team's own tools and design.
rationale.B: Optimises for effort rather than user outcomes.
rationale.C: Couples changes and makes it impossible to attribute improvements.
rationale.D: Measuring first and ranking by impact directs limited time at the problems that matter, using the trace data already available.

stem: One downstream API used by an agent fails about 5% of the time with a 503 and recovers within seconds. Today each failure ends the user's request. What is the most appropriate handling?

options.A: Retry with exponential backoff, then degrade clearly
options.B: Cache the last successful response and serve it for 24 hours
options.C: Remove the tool and have the model answer from general knowledge
options.D: Retry immediately in a tight loop until the call succeeds

rationale.A: Transient upstream failures warrant bounded retries with backoff, and a clear fallback when retries are exhausted.
rationale.B: Serves stale data for an entire day to hide a seconds-long blip.
rationale.C: Trades a transient failure for permanently ungrounded answers.
rationale.D: Hammers a struggling service and can extend the outage.

stem: Before a marketing campaign, a team wants to know whether its agent on Agent Runtime will hit platform limits, and what to check. What is the correct guidance?

options.A: Limits can only be discovered by load-testing until requests fail
options.B: Quotas do not apply to managed runtimes, so no check is needed
options.C: Review the documented quotas and request increases early
options.D: Only model quotas matter; runtime limits scale automatically without bounds

rationale.A: Documented limits exist; testing should confirm, not discover, them.
rationale.B: Managed services still have documented quotas.
rationale.C: Agent Runtime documents quota and system limits that teams should review ahead of load.
rationale.D: Both model and runtime limits apply.

stem: In long conversations, an agent slows down and eventually errors. Traces show input tokens growing with every turn because the full history is sent each time. Which change addresses the root cause?

options.A: Summarise or window the history, keeping key facts in state or memory
options.B: Start a new session every five turns, discarding earlier context
options.C: Increase the model's context limit and continue sending everything
options.D: Move the history into the system prompt instead of the messages

rationale.A: Bounding what is sent per turn, while preserving durable facts elsewhere, stops unbounded context growth.
rationale.B: Loses the conversation the user is having.
rationale.C: Postpones the failure while cost and latency keep rising.
rationale.D: Same tokens, same growth, in a different field.

stem: A platform team wants to know within minutes when an agent's quality degrades in production, not only when it errors. Which signal set is most appropriate?

options.A: Total token spend per hour
options.B: Weekly customer satisfaction survey results
options.C: Error rates, latency and sampled quality scores
options.D: CPU and memory utilisation of the agent's containers

rationale.A: Cost can stay flat while quality drops.
rationale.B: Far too slow and sparse for minutes-level detection.
rationale.C: Combining operational signals with sampled quality scoring detects degradations that never surface as errors.
rationale.D: Infrastructure health says little about answer quality.

stem: An agent on Agent Runtime serves two business units whose conversation data must remain separate, and the security team wants access enforced by the platform rather than by the agent's code. Which capability should you use?

options.A: Separate Memory Bank topics per business unit
options.B: IAM Conditions on Sessions to scope access per business unit
options.C: A tag on each session, filtered by the agent before answering
options.D: Two prompts that instruct the agent to keep the units' data apart

rationale.A: Topics steer memory extraction, not access enforcement.
rationale.B: Agent Runtime Sessions support controlling access with IAM Conditions, keeping enforcement in the platform.
rationale.C: That is application-side filtering, which the team wants to avoid.
rationale.D: Instructions are not access control.

stem: An architecture board reviews four agent proposals and must match each team's hard requirement to the right Google Cloud runtime before approving the designs. Which pairings of requirement and runtime are correct? (Choose two.)

options.A: 'Sidecar containers and GPU node pools' → Agent Runtime
options.B: 'No platform team, wants managed memory' → GKE
options.C: 'Node-level network policy' → Cloud Run
options.D: 'Existing container build pipeline, scale to zero' → Cloud Run
options.E: 'Least operational effort with managed state' → Agent Runtime

rationale.A: Those controls belong to GKE, not the managed runtime.
rationale.B: GKE demands the platform expertise the team lacks.
rationale.C: Cloud Run does not expose node-level networking controls.
rationale.D: Cloud Run serves the team's own container image and scales to zero.
rationale.E: Agent Runtime provides managed sessions, memory and observability with no infrastructure to run.

stem: An HR assistant must read each employee's own records in a third-party HR SaaS. Employees must consent individually, tokens must be refreshed without user involvement, and the agent's code must never handle raw tokens. What should you configure?

options.A: A 2-legged OAuth provider with the agent's own client credentials
options.B: An API key shared by all users, with the employee ID passed as a parameter
options.C: A service account with domain-wide delegation over the HR SaaS
options.D: A 3-legged OAuth provider in the auth manager

rationale.A: Machine-to-machine credentials cannot represent an individual employee's consent.
rationale.B: One credential for all users, and the SaaS cannot enforce per-user scope.
rationale.C: Grants standing access to everyone's records without consent.
rationale.D: 3-legged OAuth providers require user consent, and the auth manager stores the resulting tokens in a Google-managed credential vault and handles refresh.

stem: A reviewer asks how Agent Gateway and the auth manager keep end-user credentials away from agent code while still letting the agent call an external API on the user's behalf. What is the mechanism?

options.A: The agent receives a short-lived copy of the token and discards it after the call
options.B: Credentials are encrypted by the auth manager and decrypted at the gateway on egress
options.C: The gateway issues the agent a service-account key scoped to the external API
options.D: The user pastes the token into the conversation, which is redacted from logs

rationale.A: The agent still handles the raw credential, which is what the design avoids.
rationale.B: End-user credentials are encrypted by the auth manager and decrypted at the gateway, so the agent never accesses the raw credential.
rationale.C: Keys are not how user-delegated access is handled here.
rationale.D: Puts a live credential into conversation data.

stem: A bank must guarantee that a particular agent can never reach any resource in the customer-PII project, no matter what IAM roles it is granted now or later by any team. Which control provides this ceiling?

options.A: A principal access boundary policy on the agent identity
options.B: An organisation policy constraint on service account creation
options.C: An IAM allow policy that omits the PII project's resources
options.D: A VPC firewall rule blocking traffic to the project's subnets

rationale.A: A PAB limits the resources a principal can access regardless of other permissions, acting as a hard ceiling.
rationale.B: Unrelated to which resources this agent may reach.
rationale.C: Absence of a grant can be undone by any future grant.
rationale.D: Network rules do not express resource-level authorization for APIs.

stem: A platform team wants one policy object that can both allow one group of agents and deny another for the same destination, with multiple rules in a single policy, enforced on agent traffic. Which mechanism matches?

options.A: A Model Armor floor setting applied to the destination project
options.B: Two separate IAM allow and deny policies applied in sequence
options.C: A semantic governance policy written in natural language
options.D: IAM access policies with multiple rules, enforced by IAP

rationale.A: Model Armor screens content; it does not authorise agent-destination pairs.
rationale.B: That is the classic model the access policy is designed to replace for this use case.
rationale.C: Semantic governance judges intent and tool combinations rather than identity-based authorization.
rationale.D: Access policies extend the IAM model with multiple rules per policy, each able to carry allow and deny effects, and Agent Gateway uses IAP to evaluate and enforce them.

stem: Before enforcing new agent access policies, a team wants to see which calls would be denied without breaking production traffic. Which mode should they use?

options.A: Deploying the policy to a staging project only
options.B: ENFORCE with an allow-all rule at the end of the policy
options.C: DRY_RUN, which logs violations without blocking communications
options.D: Enabling audit logs and reviewing them weekly without a policy

rationale.A: Staging traffic does not reveal what production agents actually call.
rationale.B: A catch-all allow makes the policy meaningless while still enforcing earlier rules.
rationale.C: Access policy enforcement modes are DRY_RUN, which logs violations without blocking, and ENFORCE, which blocks violating communications.
rationale.D: Logs alone cannot show what the policy would have decided.

stem: During a design review, a team proposes deploying Agent Gateway without populating Agent Registry, arguing the registry is only documentation and adds onboarding work for every tool. What is the accurate explanation of why the gateway depends on the registry?

options.A: The gateway reads registry metadata to enforce granular access policies
options.B: The registry stores the gateway's TLS certificates and rotates them
options.C: The registry caches tool responses so the gateway can serve them faster
options.D: The gateway writes traffic logs into the registry for audit

rationale.A: Agent Gateway looks up metadata from Agent Registry to enforce granular access policies.
rationale.B: Certificate handling is not the registry's role.
rationale.C: The registry is a catalog, not a response cache.
rationale.D: Telemetry goes to observability, not into the catalog.

stem: A security team must guarantee a minimum screening level for every Model Armor template any project team creates, while letting teams add stricter settings for their own applications. What should they configure?

options.A: A single shared template that every application must reference
options.B: Inspect-only mode everywhere, with teams enabling blocking voluntarily
options.C: An organisation policy constraint listing required filters
options.D: Floor settings at the project level, with per-application templates on top

rationale.A: One template cannot express per-application strictness and can be bypassed by new templates.
rationale.B: Voluntary enforcement is not a guarantee.
rationale.C: Not the mechanism Model Armor provides for minimum enforcement.
rationale.D: Floor settings establish minimum requirements for all templates created at the project level, while templates configure per-application filters.

stem: A team enables Model Armor on a new agent but wants two weeks of evidence about false positives before anything is blocked. Which configuration fits, and what must they ensure?

options.A: No Model Armor for two weeks, then enable blocking directly
options.B: Inspect-only enforcement, ensuring Cloud Logging captures the findings
options.C: Inspect and block, with an allow list of known-good prompts
options.D: Inspect-only with logging disabled to reduce cost during the trial

rationale.A: Provides no data about false positives before enforcement.
rationale.B: Inspect-only logs violations without blocking, and its value depends on Cloud Logging being in place to review findings.
rationale.C: Blocks traffic during the evaluation window, which the team wanted to avoid.
rationale.D: Without logs there is no evidence to review.

stem: An agent must prevent credit card numbers and national identifiers from being sent to the model, and the compliance team also wants de-identification of some custom data types defined in their existing Sensitive Data Protection templates. What should you configure?

options.A: Basic Sensitive Data Protection, which covers custom infoTypes automatically
options.B: The responsible-AI filters, which include personal data categories
options.C: Model Armor Sensitive Data Protection in advanced mode using their SDP templates
options.D: Prompt injection detection, which blocks prompts containing card numbers

rationale.A: Basic mode covers a fixed set such as credit cards and national identifiers, not custom templates.
rationale.B: Those cover harmful content categories, not data types.
rationale.C: Basic SDP covers common identifiers; advanced mode uses Sensitive Data Protection templates for granular detection and de-identification.
rationale.D: Injection detection targets malicious instructions, not sensitive data.

stem: A product manager asks whether the team can turn off Model Armor's CSAM detection to reduce latency for an internal engineering assistant. What is the correct answer?

options.A: Yes, for internal-only applications with an approved exception
options.B: It cannot be disabled; responsible-AI protections apply by default
options.C: Yes, by setting its confidence level to low in the template
options.D: Only by switching the template to inspect-only mode

rationale.A: No such exception exists for this category.
rationale.B: Responsible-AI categories including CSAM are applied by default and cannot be disabled.
rationale.C: Confidence tuning does not remove the protection, and it cannot be disabled.
rationale.D: Enforcement mode does not remove the category.

stem: A team's Model Armor configuration blocks many legitimate prompts. They want fewer false positives while still catching clear attacks, and understand they may miss borderline cases. Which change fits?

options.A: Lower the confidence level to low and above for those filters
options.B: Switch the template to inspect and block for all categories
options.C: Raise the confidence level toward high for the noisy filters
options.D: Apply a floor setting that forces medium confidence project-wide

rationale.A: That increases false positives, the opposite of the goal.
rationale.B: Changes enforcement, not sensitivity.
rationale.C: High confidence means near-certainty with very low false positive risk, while low-and-above flags slight indications with high false positive risk.
rationale.D: Floor settings set minimums; they are not a per-filter tuning fix.

stem: A team screens both user prompts and model responses with Model Armor and wants to follow documented best practice for configuration. What should they do?

options.A: Use one template for both, so settings never diverge
options.B: Screen only responses to save tokens on the prompt side
options.C: Screen only prompts, since responses come from a trusted model
options.D: Use separate templates for prompts and for responses

rationale.A: Prompts and responses carry different risks and warrant different settings.
rationale.B: Prompt injection arrives in prompts, which would then go unscreened.
rationale.C: Responses can contain sensitive or harmful content and are screened too.
rationale.D: The documentation recommends separate Model Armor templates for user prompts and model responses.

stem: After wiring Model Armor into Agent Gateway, screening silently does not happen. Which IAM configuration should you verify?

options.A: The gateway's Model Armor callout user and user roles
options.B: That each agent identity has the Model Armor admin role
options.C: That the project's default service account has Owner
options.D: That end users hold the Model Armor viewer role

rationale.A: The Agent Gateway integration requires roles/modelarmor.calloutUser and modelarmor.user.
rationale.B: Agents do not call Model Armor directly in this integration.
rationale.C: Owner is never the right answer for a missing specific role.
rationale.D: End users are not the calling principal.

stem: A team is enabling Identity-Aware Proxy for agent authorization on an existing production gateway and wants to avoid locking out legitimate traffic on day one. What is the recommended approach?

options.A: Enable enforcement outside business hours and monitor error rates
options.B: Deploy IAP in dry-run first, then switch to enforcement
options.C: Grant all agents broad access first, then narrow it weekly
options.D: Bypass IAP for existing agents and enforce it only for new ones

rationale.A: Still blocks real traffic, just at a quieter time.
rationale.B: The gateway setup guidance is to deploy IAP in dry-run mode first so the configuration can be validated before enforcement.
rationale.C: Starts from an insecure state in production.
rationale.D: Leaves the majority of traffic ungoverned indefinitely.

stem: A CISO discovers teams have deployed agents nobody tracks, some calling external APIs. She wants an inventory plus enforceable limits on what agents may reach. Which combination addresses both?

options.A: Billing alerts on model spend per project
options.B: A spreadsheet inventory maintained by each team lead monthly
options.C: Model Armor templates applied to every project
options.D: Agent Registry for inventory, gateway policies to enforce

rationale.A: Cost signals do not reveal or control agent behaviour.
rationale.B: Manual inventories drift and enforce nothing.
rationale.C: Content screening does not inventory agents or limit destinations.
rationale.D: The registry catalogs agents, tools and MCP servers, and the gateway enforces access policy using that metadata.

stem: An auditor asks who did what when an agent deleted a record on a user's behalf. The company uses Agent Identity. What does the audit trail show?

options.A: Both the agent's identity and the user's identity for the action
options.B: Only the end user, since the agent acts purely as a proxy
options.C: Only the project and the API method invoked
options.D: Only the shared service account used by the agent fleet

rationale.A: When agents act on behalf of users, logs show both the agent's and the user's identities.
rationale.B: The acting agent is recorded as well.
rationale.C: Identity attribution is richer than that with agent identities.
rationale.D: Agent identities replace shared service accounts precisely to avoid this.

stem: A compliance officer wants to express, in plain English, that an agent may look up a customer's balance but must never move money to an account added in the last 24 hours. Which capability supports this, and what is a practical limit to know?

options.A: Model Armor custom filters, limited to 4 MB of policy text
options.B: IAM conditions with CEL expressions, limited to 5,000 characters
options.C: Natural-language constraints, capped at 5,000 characters
options.D: Agent Registry endpoint descriptions, limited to 1,024 characters

rationale.A: The 4 MB figure is Model Armor's content size limit, and it does not express business rules.
rationale.B: CEL is not plain English and does not evaluate intent.
rationale.C: Natural Language Constraints let rules be written in plain English at the gateway, with a documented limit of 5,000 characters.
rationale.D: Descriptions document entries; they do not enforce rules.

stem: During a security review, a team proposes enforcing all tool-access rules by listing them in the agent's system prompt, arguing the model follows instructions reliably. What is the strongest objection?

options.A: Prompts are not an enforcement boundary; policy must sit outside the model
options.B: Prompts cannot be long enough to hold all the rules
options.C: Prompts cannot be version-controlled with the rest of the configuration
options.D: Prompt rules make the model slower because of extra tokens

rationale.A: Any instruction in the prompt can be overridden by injection or model error, so authorization belongs in identity, policy and gateway controls.
rationale.B: Length is a minor issue compared with the lack of enforcement.
rationale.C: They can be; the problem is that they do not enforce anything.
rationale.D: Cost and latency are secondary to the security gap.

stem: A company wants agent traffic subject to its existing data-exfiltration perimeter, with ingress and egress rules that name agents specifically. Which statement is correct?

options.A: Perimeters apply only to human users, not to workloads
options.B: Agents must run outside perimeters because certificates rotate daily
options.C: VPC Service Controls cannot reference agents, only service accounts
options.D: Agent Identity integrates with VPC Service Controls for perimeter protection

rationale.A: VPC-SC governs API access by principals including workloads.
rationale.B: Rotation does not conflict with perimeter membership.
rationale.C: Agent identities can be named in perimeter rules.
rationale.D: Agent Identity is integrated with policy systems including IAM, PAB and VPC Service Controls, with agent principals usable in perimeter rules.

stem: An organisation wants a documented process before any new tool is exposed to production agents: security review, an owner, and registration so policy can be applied. A team objects that this slows delivery. What is the best compromise?

options.A: Allow any tool in production and review after the first incident
options.B: Require full architecture review for every tool regardless of risk
options.C: Lightweight review with registration, fast-tracked for read-only
options.D: Let each team self-certify without central registration

rationale.A: Accepts unbounded risk as the default.
rationale.B: The friction the team objects to, with little added safety for read-only tools.
rationale.C: Risk-proportionate review keeps the governance requirement while removing friction for low-risk, read-only capabilities.
rationale.D: Leaves no inventory and no way to apply policy.

stem: A developer asks how outbound credentials from the auth manager reach an MCP tool call made by their ADK agent, without them writing credential code. What is the mechanism?

options.A: The MCP server reads the user's cookie from the browser session
options.B: The auth manager integrates with ADK to inject auth headers into tool and MCP calls
options.C: Credentials are embedded into the agent's container image at build time
options.D: The developer fetches the token from Secret Manager in a before_tool_callback

rationale.A: Server-side agents do not proxy browser cookies.
rationale.B: The auth manager integrates natively with ADK to retrieve and inject outbound authentication headers such as Authorization or an API key header into tool and MCP server invocations.
rationale.C: Baked-in secrets cannot represent per-user consent and are a leak risk.
rationale.D: That is manual credential handling, which the auth manager removes.

stem: A security architect reviews how an agent's credentials are protected when its traffic passes through Agent Gateway, and asks what stops a stolen token from being replayed by another client. What does the platform provide?

options.A: DPoP-bound credentials on top of mTLS, so tokens are double-bound
options.B: Short token lifetimes of five minutes, after which replay fails
options.C: IP allow-lists on the gateway that reject unknown source addresses
options.D: Encryption of the token at rest in Secret Manager

rationale.A: When interacting through Agent Gateway, agents use Demonstrating Proof of Possession, creating double-bound credentials alongside mTLS certificates.
rationale.B: Shortening lifetimes narrows the window but does not bind the token to its holder.
rationale.C: Network filtering is coarse and fails for shared egress addresses.
rationale.D: Protects storage, not use of a token that has already been obtained.

stem: A finance owner asks how Model Armor costs will scale as agent traffic grows, so the team can forecast next quarter's budget. What is the basis for its pricing?

options.A: The number of templates and floor settings configured in the project
options.B: The total number of tokens in the prompts and responses screened
options.C: The number of violations detected and blocked each month
options.D: A flat monthly fee for each agent that has screening enabled

rationale.A: Configuration objects are not the billing unit.
rationale.B: Model Armor uses the total number of tokens in AI prompts and responses for pricing purposes.
rationale.C: Blocked findings are not the unit of charge.
rationale.D: Pricing is usage-based on tokens, not per agent.

stem: A platform team needs one policy that allows an agent group to reach an internal API only when the request targets a specific resource path, and denies everything else for that group. How are such rules expressed in IAM access policies?

options.A: As a list of allowed URLs in the gateway's YAML configuration file
options.B: As natural-language sentences evaluated by a model at request time
options.C: As rules with allow or deny effects and CEL-based conditions on the destination
options.D: As firewall rules attached to the destination's subnet

rationale.A: Policy is expressed as IAM access policy rules, not gateway URL lists.
rationale.B: That describes semantic governance, not identity-based access policies.
rationale.C: Each rule in an access policy contains an effect and CEL-based conditions specifying destination resources and access criteria.
rationale.D: Network rules cannot express resource-path conditions for API calls.

stem: A security team wants every custom MCP server used in production to be subject to central policy. A developer says their server is internal, so registration is unnecessary. What is the correct position?

options.A: Internal servers inherit the project's policies automatically once deployed
options.B: Registration only matters for servers exposed to the public internet
options.C: The gateway discovers MCP servers by scanning the VPC on a schedule
options.D: Custom and external MCP servers must be registered explicitly to be governed

rationale.A: Deployment alone does not place a server under gateway policy.
rationale.B: Governance applies to internal tools as well.
rationale.C: There is no such discovery scan.
rationale.D: Official Google Cloud remote MCP servers are ingested automatically, but external or custom servers must be registered explicitly for discovery and governance.

stem: An operations agent can restart services, open firewall ports and post to the company's public status page. Leadership wants automation but refuses unattended risk on irreversible or public actions. Which design best balances this?

options.A: Require human approval for every action the agent takes
options.B: Automate everything and send a notification after each action
options.C: Automate everything during business hours and require approval at night
options.D: Require human confirmation for irreversible and public actions, automate the rest

rationale.A: Removes the benefit of automation and trains reviewers to click through.
rationale.B: Notification after an irreversible public action is too late.
rationale.C: Risk depends on the action, not the time of day.
rationale.D: Human-in-the-loop should gate consequential actions while low-risk steps stay automated, which is the pattern the guide describes.

stem: A team implementing human-in-the-loop in ADK wants the agent to pause at a specific tool, show the reviewer what will happen, and continue only after approval, with no external workflow engine. What should they use?

options.A: A Cloud Workflows step that calls the agent back after approval
options.B: An instruction telling the agent to wait for the word 'approved'
options.C: ADK tool confirmation, which pauses the tool until the user responds
options.D: A Pub/Sub topic the reviewer publishes to, polled by the agent

rationale.A: Adds the external engine the team wanted to avoid.
rationale.B: The model can proceed anyway; nothing technically pauses the tool.
rationale.C: ADK's tool confirmation feature lets a tool pause execution and interact with a user for confirmation before proceeding.
rationale.D: Custom plumbing for a built-in capability.

stem: A retail agent faces three risks: users trying prompt injection through product reviews, the agent occasionally drafting offensive replies, and the risk of it emailing customer lists externally. Which layered design addresses all three?

options.A: A single system prompt that forbids all three behaviours
options.B: Model Armor for content, gateway policy on the email tool
options.C: Gateway policy alone, denying all external destinations
options.D: Model Armor alone, configured with inspect and block for every category

rationale.A: Prompts do not enforce any of the three.
rationale.B: Content screening handles injection and responsible-AI categories, while authorization policy at the gateway constrains which tools and destinations are reachable.
rationale.C: Blocks legitimate email and leaves injection and harmful content unscreened.
rationale.D: Screening does not stop an authorised tool from sending data externally.

stem: A security architect asks which control specifically addresses prompt-injection risks that arrive through MCP tool responses rather than through user messages. What should you name?

options.A: Model Armor screening on the gateway path, which covers MCP injection risks
options.B: Restricting the agent to read-only tools
options.C: Input validation on the user's chat message before it reaches the model
options.D: A rate limit on the MCP server to slow down attackers

rationale.A: Agent Gateway integrates Model Armor to protect against risks such as MCP prompt injection attacks.
rationale.B: Reduces blast radius but does not detect the injection.
rationale.C: The injection arrives in tool output, not the user message.
rationale.D: Throttling does not neutralise injected instructions.

stem: A support agent's transcripts are stored for quality review, and the privacy team wants identifiers removed from stored transcripts while keeping them readable for analysis. Which service handles this?

options.A: Cloud Logging exclusion filters on the transcript sink
options.B: Agent Gateway egress policy on the storage API
options.C: Sensitive Data Protection de-identification
options.D: Model Armor floor settings applied to the storage bucket

rationale.A: Excluding logs discards data instead of de-identifying transcripts.
rationale.B: Authorization does not transform stored content.
rationale.C: Sensitive Data Protection inspects data for sensitive elements and can de-identify it while preserving analytical utility.
rationale.D: Model Armor screens prompts and responses in the request path, not stored objects.

stem: An agent queries a data warehouse on behalf of employees. Today it uses one service account with broad access and filters rows in code by the caller's email. Security calls this a critical finding. What is the correct architecture?

options.A: Create one service account per employee, provisioned by a nightly job
options.B: Propagate the user's identity so the warehouse enforces their permissions
options.C: Encrypt query results so only the requesting employee can read them
options.D: Keep the service account but move filtering into a hardened tool wrapper

rationale.A: Operationally fragile and still not the user's own identity.
rationale.B: Identity propagation makes the downstream system enforce per-user access instead of trusting application-side filtering.
rationale.C: The agent could still retrieve data the employee may not access.
rationale.D: Still one over-privileged identity, with enforcement in application code.

stem: A finance agent asks for approval on every generated journal entry. Reviewers approve 400 entries a day and admit they click approve without reading. Which change most improves real control?

options.A: Replace approval with a daily report of what the agent posted
options.B: Require two approvers for every entry
options.C: Add a five-second delay before the approve button becomes active
options.D: Auto-approve low-risk entries; route exceptions with context

rationale.A: Removes the control entirely for high-risk entries.
rationale.B: Doubles the rubber-stamping rather than reducing volume.
rationale.C: Slows clicks without improving judgement.
rationale.D: Concentrating human attention on genuinely risky cases restores meaningful review instead of rubber-stamping.

stem: A claims agent accepts photo uploads and the team wants Model Armor to screen them. Their deployment is in an Asian region and users often attach three photos per message. What should they expect?

options.A: Image screening supports one image per request and US or EU multi-regions
options.B: Images are screened in every region, with up to ten per request
options.C: Images are converted to text by OCR and screened as documents anywhere
options.D: Image screening requires the advanced Sensitive Data Protection mode

rationale.A: Model Armor image screening is supported only in US and EU multi-regions and allows a maximum of one image per request.
rationale.B: Contradicts the documented region and per-request limits.
rationale.C: Document screening is integrated only with Gemini Enterprise, and image limits still apply.
rationale.D: SDP mode relates to sensitive data types, not image support.

stem: A research agent summarises web pages and sometimes surfaces links from untrusted sources. The team wants malicious links flagged. What should they know about Model Armor's malicious URL detection?

options.A: It blocks all external URLs by default in every template
options.B: It validates TLS certificates for each linked domain
options.C: It scans the first 256 URLs per request
options.D: It rewrites malicious URLs so users cannot click them

rationale.A: Filters are configurable and do not blanket-block URLs.
rationale.B: Certificate validation is not what this filter does.
rationale.C: Malicious URL detection scans URLs to identify whether they are malicious, with a documented limit of the first 256 URLs.
rationale.D: Detection flags content; rewriting is not the described behaviour.

stem: An agent that reconciles invoices needs read access to an accounting API and write access to a single reporting table. The team plans to reuse an existing identity that already has broad finance permissions 'to save time'. What should the reviewer require?

options.A: The existing identity, with Model Armor enabled on the agent
options.B: The existing identity, with an IAM condition limiting it to business hours
options.C: The existing identity, with all actions logged for later review
options.D: A dedicated identity for this agent with only those two permissions

rationale.A: Content screening does not limit authorised API access.
rationale.B: Time conditions do not reduce the scope of what it can reach.
rationale.C: Detection after the fact is not prevention.
rationale.D: Per-agent identities with narrowly scoped permissions bound the blast radius if the agent is manipulated.

stem: An analytics agent runs model-generated Python over customer data. Which combination of controls best limits the damage if the generated code is malicious or buggy? (Choose two.)

options.A: Log the generated code and review it weekly
options.B: Execute the code in an isolated sandbox with no standing credentials
options.C: Ask the model to review its own code for safety before running it
options.D: Restrict egress from the execution environment to approved destinations
options.E: Run the code with the agent's own service account for simplicity

rationale.A: After-the-fact review does not prevent the damage.
rationale.B: Isolation and credential-free execution prevent generated code from reaching other systems.
rationale.C: Self-review by the same system that wrote the code is not a control.
rationale.D: Network restrictions stop exfiltration even if the code runs successfully.
rationale.E: Gives generated code the agent's full permissions.

stem: A platform team must show auditors that every call an agent makes to an internal API carries both the agent's authenticated identity and the end user it acts for, with central telemetry. Which architecture satisfies this?

options.A: Use one gateway service account and correlate calls by timestamp
options.B: Route calls through Agent Gateway with agent identities
options.C: Add the user's email as a header the internal API trusts
options.D: Have each agent write its own audit log entry before calling the API

rationale.A: Timestamps do not attribute identity.
rationale.B: The gateway authenticates agent identities using SPIFFE-based principals secured with mTLS and DPoP, and exports observability telemetry for all agent interactions.
rationale.C: An unverified header is trivially spoofed.
rationale.D: Self-reported logs are unauthenticated and can be omitted.

stem: A retailer is deciding where to place human-in-the-loop checkpoints in its customer-service agent, and wants them only where they are justified, because each checkpoint adds handling time. Which of these actions most clearly warrants a checkpoint?

options.A: Issuing a refund above the agent's automatic threshold
options.B: Summarising the conversation for the transcript
options.C: Searching the knowledge base for a policy article
options.D: Looking up the customer's order history

rationale.A: Moving money is consequential and hard to reverse, which is the classic criterion for human approval.
rationale.B: Internal, reversible and low risk.
rationale.C: Read-only retrieval with no side effects.
rationale.D: A read-only action with no lasting effect.

stem: Each tool an agent holds is individually safe: read customer records, generate a document, send email. Security is concerned about them being chained into a data-exfiltration path. Which control is designed for this risk?

options.A: Semantic governance policies on tool combinations
options.B: Per-tool IAM permissions reviewed quarterly
options.C: Rate limiting the email tool to ten messages per hour
options.D: Model Armor responsible-AI filters on the generated document

rationale.A: Semantic governance adds context-aware controls protecting against toxic combinations of tools, evaluated against user intent before execution.
rationale.B: Each tool is individually approved; the risk is their combination.
rationale.C: A slow exfiltration path is still an exfiltration path.
rationale.D: Content screening does not evaluate tool sequences against intent.

stem: An architect claims that because Agent Gateway enforces authorization, the team does not need least-privilege identities for agents. What is the best response?

options.A: Disagree: IAM alone is enough, so the gateway can be removed
options.B: Keep both: they fail differently and cover different paths
options.C: Agree, provided the gateway runs in enforce mode with logging
options.D: Agree: a single enforcement point is simpler and sufficient

rationale.A: IAM does not provide the gateway's content screening or intent-aware policy.
rationale.B: Layered controls mean a misconfiguration or bypass in one does not grant unrestricted access.
rationale.C: Enforcement mode does not cover calls that never traverse the gateway.
rationale.D: One control becomes a single point of failure.

stem: An agent sends a customer's full profile, including national ID and full address, to a third-party shipping-rate API that only needs the destination postcode and parcel weight. What should the reviewer require?

options.A: Keep the payload but encrypt it in transit with TLS 1.3
options.B: Keep the payload but strip identifiers from the response
options.C: Send only the postcode and weight, minimising what leaves the boundary
options.D: Keep the payload and add a data processing agreement with the vendor

rationale.A: Transport encryption does not stop the third party from receiving the data.
rationale.B: The sensitive data has already been sent.
rationale.C: Data minimisation reduces exposure at the integration boundary and is the simplest durable fix.
rationale.D: Contracts manage liability; they do not reduce exposure.

stem: A team logs full prompts and responses for debugging, including customer messages that contain payment details. Compliance objects. Which change preserves debuggability with the least data risk?

options.A: Stop logging prompts and responses entirely
options.B: Shorten log retention to seven days and keep full content
options.C: Keep full logs but restrict access to the security team
options.D: Redact sensitive fields, keeping correlation identifiers

rationale.A: Removes the ability to debug agent behaviour.
rationale.B: Reduces the window but not the exposure.
rationale.C: Sensitive data is still retained broadly and remains a breach risk.
rationale.D: Redaction with identifiers keeps traces useful for debugging while removing the sensitive content from logs.

stem: After enabling stricter agent policies, one agent's calls to an approved partner API start failing while other agents are unaffected. An engineer proposes granting that agent broad permissions to unblock the release today. What should the reviewer require instead?

options.A: Route that agent's traffic around the gateway with a direct egress rule
options.B: Temporarily disable policy enforcement for that project until after the release
options.C: Diagnose the denial in the logs and grant only the missing permission
options.D: Grant the agent the Editor role and schedule a review for next quarter

rationale.A: Bypasses the control point entirely and hides the traffic.
rationale.B: Removes governance for every agent in the project.
rationale.C: Gateway denials identify the agent, destination and decision, so the fix is a targeted grant rather than broad access.
rationale.D: Broad standing access is what the reviewer must prevent.

stem: An agent is asked to 'clean up old records' and proposes calling a bulk delete tool across all customers. The tool call is technically permitted by IAM. Which control evaluates whether the action matches the user's actual intent before it runs?

options.A: Model Armor prompt injection detection on the user's message
options.B: A semantic governance policy that returns allow or deny with a rationale
options.C: An after-tool callback that logs what was deleted
options.D: An IAM deny policy on the bulk delete tool for that agent

rationale.A: The message is not an injection; the issue is scope of the action.
rationale.B: Semantic governance acts as a runtime gate that reads every proposed tool call against the prompt, conversation and policies, returning allow or deny before the tool executes.
rationale.C: Runs after the deletion has happened.
rationale.D: Blocks the tool outright, including legitimate scoped use.

stem: A regulator asks a bank to demonstrate, for a sample of automated decisions, who approved them and what the approver saw. The agent currently records only that a human clicked approve. What should be added?

options.A: Require two approvers so the decision is harder to dispute
options.B: Increase log retention for the existing approval events to seven years
options.C: Store the model's reasoning text as the record of the decision
options.D: Record the action, the context shown and the approver identity with each decision

rationale.A: More approvers without context does not answer the regulator's question.
rationale.B: Keeping insufficient records longer does not make them sufficient.
rationale.C: Model reasoning is not evidence of human review.
rationale.D: An auditable human-in-the-loop trail must capture what was presented, who decided and what was decided, not merely that approval occurred.

stem: An agent that answers HR policy questions is also given a tool that can update employee records, because 'it may be useful later'. Which principle does this violate, and what should happen?

options.A: Least privilege: remove the tool until a use case justifies it
options.B: Data minimisation: keep the tool but limit the fields it returns
options.C: Defence in depth: keep the tool but add Model Armor screening
options.D: Separation of duties: keep the tool but require a second agent to approve

rationale.A: Capabilities an agent does not need expand the blast radius of prompt injection or model error and should not be attached speculatively.
rationale.B: The risk is the write capability, not the fields read.
rationale.C: Screening content does not stop an authorised write the agent decides to make.
rationale.D: Adds cost and complexity for a capability that is not needed at all.
